===== [p413-413] STEP 5 - CONFIRMING THAT UTILITY SOURCES MEET REQUIREMENTS > TEMPERATURE-CONTROLLED WATER (2块) =====
--[p413]-- TEMPERATURE-CONTROLLED WATER
The coolant in (18) and coolant out (17) permit the cycling of temperaturecontrolled water through the polish table for a temperature-controlled polishing process. Both connections require mating to the machine’s 3/4- inch PVC threaded pipe joints. The pressure regulator adjusts the pressure of the liquid flowing through the loop. The coolant in (18) and coolant out (17) must be connected to the temperature control unit.
--[p413]-- A bypass valve, coolant bypass (19), mounted at the rear of the machine, provides overpressure protection for the polish table. If coolant back pressure rises above 10 PSI, the coolant bypass valve opens and dumps to the table drain (12) to prevent damage to the table.

===== [p125-126] CALIBRATION/CONFIGURATION CHANGES > USER INPUT (6块) =====
--[p125]-- USER INPUT
Screen Function Key Labels and Function Keys: The screen function key labels along the bottom of the screen describe choices possible at the currently displayed menu. A choice is available if the password level permits it and the machine's operation permits it. Any unavailable choice will be "ghosted".
The menu selection functions and Abort/Reset choice are always available and are never "ghosted".
--[p126]-- Abort/Reset Function Key: The Abort/Reset choice always shows as the F10 key. F10 can be used to abort whatever the machine is doing and return everything to its default status (sprays off, servo moves stopped, etc.)
When first pressed, a warning will show which permits escaping (canceling the abort request). If pressed again, the abort/reset occurs. This second press confirmation prevents an unwanted abort/reset if F10 is accidentally pressed.
--[p125]-- Enter Choice causes the currently showing choice to be confirmed and the cursor color to change back to yellow.
Escape by either the Escape key, moving the cursor off the item, or selecting a menu.
Password Permission Levels: Illustrations of the menu screens used in the 6DS-SP Operations and Maintenance manuals include the password permission level(s) required for changing the available menu selections. All selections are available for viewing at all password levels.
--[p125]-- When the first number entry key is pressed, the field color will change to red, indicating the value is in the process of being input by the user but is not yet confirmed by pressing the Enter key. An unconfirmed value can still be edited. When the Enter key is pressed, the value showing is confirmed, and the cursor color changes back to yellow.
Escape by using the Escape key, moving the cursor off the item, or selecting a menu.
--[p125]-- Entering numbers: Numbers are conventionally entered using numerals, the decimal, the hyphen, and the Enter key. The Backspace and Escape keys can also be used.
Sometimes numbers are entered into "fields" in the menu area, and sometimes they are entered at the end of the prompt line.
Number entry areas will first be yellow.
--[p125]-- (The rules controlling number entry also apply for entering letters when creating a recipe name.)
Entering Choices: If a menu has word choices in any fields, the View Choice and Enter Choice function keys will show.
View Choice permits scrolling through the choices (usually there are only two or three choices). When using View Choice, the field color will change from yellow to red which means a new choice is showing but is not yet confirmed.

Design emphasis has focused on maximizing potential polishing results while incorporating versatility, reliability, and simplicity of operation.

===== [p49-387] GALLIUM ARSENIDE AND GERMANIUM USE > REACTIVITY WARNING (2块) =====
--[p387]-- REACTIVITY WARNING
Gallium arsenide is incompatible with steam, acids, acid fumes, and quartz. When gallium arsenide decomposes and/or reacts with incompatible substances, poisonous arsine gas and hazardous oxides of gallium and arsenic are produced. Additionally, molten gallium arsenide attacks quartz.
See Section 6 of the gallium arsenide MSDS for additional information.

===== [p46-384] APPENDIX TO LOCKOUT SAFETY PROCEDURE > Removal of Lockout/Tagout Devices (4块) =====
--[p384]-- Removal of Lockout/Tagout Devices
Before lockout or tagout devices are removed, the authorized employee shall ensure that non-essential items are removed and machine components are operationally intact. The area should be checked to ensure all employees are safely positioned or removed and all affected employees notified that lockout/tagout devices have been removed. The lockout/tagout device must be removed by the person who applied the device.
--[p384]-- If the person who applied the device is not available, the device may be removed by another employee if the employer has established a specific procedure and training for this. When group lockout/tagout devices are used, a procedure equivalent to the personal lockout/tagout system should be followed [29 CFR 1910.147 (f) (3)].
--[p46]-- If the person who applied the device is not available, the device may be removed by another employee if the employer has established a specific procedure and training for this. When group lockout/tagout devices are used, a procedure equivalent to the personal lockout/tagout system should be followed [29 CFR 1910.147 (f) (3)].

===== [p255-255] ADDITIONAL FEATURES AT THE MACHINE PARAMETERS MENU > EXPANDED PASSWORD PROTECTION: (3块) =====
--[p255]-- EXPANDED PASSWORD PROTECTION:
Three password levels are offered: Operator, Engineer, and Maintenance.
The Operator level permits recipe retrieval but does not permit any changes to any menus (with the exception of optional time and backpressure changes described below).
The Engineer level allows changes to process parameters and access to the manual control menu. The Maintenance level allows access to all menus.
Passwords are 1 to 8 digit numbers. (Alpha characters cannot be used.)
--[p255]-- These password levels define access to function key choices on the various menus. They are not used for any other purpose. Password levels are set in the Password Menu.
The "Operator" level does not require a password and will immediately be set if the Set to 'Oper' function key is pressed.
The Engineer and Maintenance levels can optionally have password protection.
--[p255]-- If no passwords have been entered for a password level, then that level will be immediately be set when its "set to" function key is pressed. However, if passwords exists, then the prompt line will ask for one.
Up to 15 passwords can exist for the Engineer level and 15 for the Maintenance level.

===== [p117-117] MENU GROUPING AND RECIPE DEFINITION > RECIPE DEFINITION (3块) =====
--[p117]-- (Machine settings which are seldom or never changed reside in the Calibration/Configuration Menu.)
The maintenance menus work together as a group. If any change is made in the Manual Control Menu, the status line will show Manual Mode. If any change is made in the Diagnostic Menu, the status line will show Diag Mode. As long as menu selection involves only the maintenance menus, the changes will remain.
--[p117]-- However, if a door is opened in the manual mode, choices in the section protected by the door's interlock will be cancelled. Finally, if a non-maintenance menu is selected, an automatic abort/reset will occur to clear the changes and reset the machine back to normal.
--[p117]-- RECIPE DEFINITION
The recipe is defined as everything seen in the Slurry Flush Menu and everything in the "parameter" menus. (Note: With pre-4.00 software, only polish parameter values were saved as the recipe.) Since everything in these menus can affect processing in some way, they are now included in the recipe.
The Machine Setup Menu contains machine setups that are commonly changed as part of machine operation but are not process related.

===== [p137-137] MENUS USED IN BASIC OPERATION > PRESETTABLE WAFER POLISH COUNT: (2块) =====
--[p137]-- PRESETTABLE WAFER POLISH COUNT:
This feature permits the operator to set the machine to polish a finite number of wafers and stop automatically. Presettable wafer polish count is applicable in the automatic (cassette to cassette) mode only.
Function key choices No. of Wafers and ALL Wafers show on the Auto Polish Menu and the Polish Parameters Menu.
If No. of Wafers is selected, the prompt line will ask for a number of wafers from 1 to 50.
--[p137]-- Once entered, this value will show in the Wfrs status area of the screen. This value will be decremented by the number of spindles used each time a polishing cycle starts. When it reaches zero, the machine status will automatically change from In Polish Cycle to Finishing Cycle. When the machine stops, the Wfrs status will automatically switch back to ALL.
If the machine is interrupted, it will remember the wafer count and resume counting down when polishing is restarted.
If All Wafers is selected, the Wfrs status will display All and the machine will polish wafers indefinitely.

--[p452]-- ELEVATOR ASSEMBLY
The elevator assembly, located at the left of the machine, consists of two functional units, send and receive. The left and right send elevators, located at the rear of the machine, raise and lower cassettes loaded with unprocessed wafers. The left and right receive elevators, located near the middle of the machine, raise and lower cassettes loaded with processed wafers.
The elevator back support houses a polymer nut and two pillow block bearings.
--[p452]-- The bearings travel on a rail supported by the framework of the elevator slide assembly. The polymer nut is stationary, and a lead screw is rotated inside the nut. The lead screw is supported at both ends by bearings mounted on the slide assembly. The lead screw is belt-driven by a brushless DC motor with a tooth belt and two pulleys.
The motor has uses encoder feedback to monitor speed and position.
--[p83]-- The light sensor detection is active only if the elevator arm is lowered onto a cassette.
When the elevator access door is closed, the elevator automatic fill and drain valve feature automatically keeps the elevator tanks filled with water whenever cassettes are present on the elevators. If an elevator arm is lifted, its tank will begin draining. The drain valve will remain open as long as the arm is lifted. If the elevator had been filling, the fill valve will now close.
--[p83]-- The elevators sit in tanks supplied with water from an air operated valve controlled by a solenoid valve mounted on the valve panel located at the lower left side of the machine.
The elevator light sensor option detects any wafer not correctly (and safely) positioned in its cassette slot. The incorrectly positioned wafer will break an invisible infrared light beam.

===== [p450-450] MECHANICAL DESCRIPTION > 27. If carrier cleaning is enabled: (1块) =====

a. The shuttle moves backward to its rear position.
b. The spindles move down into the cleaning stations.
c. The spindles begin rotating as the carrier cleaning cycle begins.
d. When the cleaning cycle is finished, the spindles move up.
e. The shuttle moves forward.
f. The machine begins the next auto cycle.

===== [p85-454] MECHANICAL DESCRIPTION > ROBOT ASSEMBLY (12块) =====
--[p85]-- The robot rotational (theta) axis is belt driven by a brushless DC motor (mounted inside the robot assembly), two pulleys, and a tooth belt. An inductive sensor located inside the housing “homes” the theta axis. Encoder feedback monitors position and speed.
The robot radial axis (also belt driven by a brushless DC motor, two pulleys, and a tooth belt) is mounted on a spindle located in the end of the theta axis housing. The spindle is driven by two pulleys and a belt.
--[p454]-- ROBOT ASSEMBLY
Supported by a slide assembly, the robot travels between the left elevators and the right load station, stopping at each elevator and load station (a range of approximately three feet). The slide assembly is comprised of two hardened steel rails and a lead screw supported at both ends. On the right end of the lead screw, a brushless DC motor is connected by direct drive through a flexible coupling to the lead screw.
--[p454]-- The belt and pulleys are driven by a shaft (driven by two more pulleys, a belt, and a motor) extending down inside the robot assembly. An inductive sensor located on the underneath side of the housing “homes” the radial axis. Encoder feedback monitors position and speed.
The robot’s radial and theta axes permit it to reach into wafer cassettes and out over the load stations, positioning an end effector located on the theta axis over a wafer.
--[p85]-- The belt and pulleys are driven by a shaft (driven by two more pulleys, a belt, and a motor) extending down inside the robot assembly. An inductive sensor located on the underneath side of the housing “homes” the radial axis. Encoder feedback monitors position and speed.
The robot’s radial and theta axes permit it to reach into wafer cassettes and out over the load stations, positioning an end effector located on the theta axis over a wafer.
--[p85]-- A stationary lead screw (located inside a nut mounted in two bearings on the framework of the robot) is rotated by a brushless DC motor driving a tooth belt and two pulleys, causing upward and downward movement of the robot. Encoder feedback monitors position and speed. The Z-axis has a single inductive sensor located at the middle range of travel and functioning as a “home” switch.
--[p454]-- The end effector is a vacuum chuck fitted into the end of the theta axis. The vacuum chuck picks up and deposits wafers to and from elevators and load stations. The end effector is equipped with a vacuum switch, located inside the housing, to sense when the robot has taken vacuum on a wafer.
--[p454]-- A stationary lead screw (located inside a nut mounted in two bearings on the framework of the robot) is rotated by a brushless DC motor driving a tooth belt and two pulleys, causing upward and downward movement of the robot. Encoder feedback monitors position and speed. The Z-axis has a single inductive sensor located at the middle range of travel and functioning as a “home” switch.
--[p454]-- Four linear pillow block bearings mounted underneath the robot base slide on the hardened steel rails. The lead screw is rotated within a stationary polymer nut located underneath the robot base, causing linear movement of the robot. Encoder feedback monitors position and speed.
The robot’s Z-axis provides up and down linear travel. Located inside the rectangular housing, the Z-axis has a backplate mounted with three linear bearings mounted on a spine shaft at the center of the housing.
--[p85]-- The end effector is a vacuum chuck fitted into the end of the theta axis. The vacuum chuck picks up and deposits wafers to and from elevators and load stations. ===== [p91-460] CONDITIONING ARM DOWN FORCE ASSEMBLY (10块) =====
--[p91]-- CONDITIONING ARM DOWN FORCE ASSEMBLY
The servo-controlled conditioning arm down force feature provides programmable down force for the pad conditioning device.
The conditioning arm device assembly consists of a circular rotating device (with programmable rotational speed) which applies a downward force upon the polish table while being driven linearly by a linear drive DC motor from the middle of the polish table to its circumference (or vice versa) for a conditioning cycle.
--[p91]-- At the end of a cycle, the conditioning assembly parks itself off the polish table to the right. A magnet in the linear drive mechanism homes the arm, using encoder feedback to determine its inner, outer, and park positions. A pneumatic cylinder at the base of the arm assembly shaft raises the entire assembly to move the conditioning device off the polish table or lowers it to apply a regulated downward pressure upon the surface of the polish table.
--[p91]-- When the arm is at the table, a second air cylinder, together with a load cell and an electro-pneumatic regulator, raises and lowers the device itself, producing and controlling conditioning down force. The second air cylinder’s function is programmable in software.
The load cell senses the amount of force applied and generates an analog voltage signal proportional to the amount of force. This signal is amplified and transmitted to the control computer through an analog input channel.
--[p460]-- The control computer receives the information and compares it to the programmed value of required device down force. The control computer regulates the applied force by regulating the air flow to the air cylinder with the electro-pneumatic regulator. The control computer generates an analog voltage signal for the electropneumatic regulator, and the regulator adjusts the air pressure in proportion to the voltage level of the signal.
--[p91]-- Together the control computer, load cell, and electro-pneumatic regulator form a closed loop controller to maintain the downward conditioning force within 2% of the programmed force value in pressure mode.
The programmable functions of the conditioning arm are controlled at the Sweep Parameters and Conditioning/Cleaning Parameters Menus.
--[p460]-- CONDITIONING ARM DOWN FORCE ASSEMBLY
The servo-controlled conditioning arm down force feature provides programmable down force for the pad conditioning device.
The conditioning arm device assembly consists of a circular rotating device (with programmable rotational speed) which applies a downward force upon the polish table while being driven linearly by a linear drive DC motor from the middle of the polish table to its circumference (or vice versa) for a conditioning cycle.

--[p252]-- PASSWORD MENU
This menu allows changing the password level, creating passwords, and deleting passwords. There are three password levels: "Operator", "Engineer", and "Maintenance". These levels determine which function key choices are available for each menu.
The "Operator" level does not require a password and permits machine operation but not recipe changes or maintenance. The machine always powers up in the operator level.
--[p252]-- The "Engineer" level may require an engineer password and permits operation and recipe changes but not maintenance. If no engineer passwords exist, the engineer password level will be immediately set if the function key Set to 'Engr' is pressed.
The "Maintenance" level may require a maintenance password and permits access to all functions. If no maintenance passwords exist, the ,Maintenance password level will be immediately set if the function key Set to 'Maint' is pressed.

--[p104]-- C. POLISH CYCLE SEQUENCE
1. The spindles move down to the table.
2. The polishing sequence begins.

4. Spindle down force and back pressure on the wafer start to ramp up.
5. The cycle times out.
6. Down force is reduced to near zero.
7. Back pressure vacuum to the wafer is turned on.
8. When back pressure vacuum reaches the required level, the spindles lift off the table.

f. Down force is reduced to near zero.
g. Back pressure vacuum to the wafer is turned on.
h. When back pressure vacuum reaches the required level, the spindles lift off the table.

===== [p28-366] ABOUT THE MODEL 6DS-SP PLANARIZER > MECHANICAL COMPONENTS (6块) =====
--[p28]-- MECHANICAL COMPONENTS
The machine consists of three major mechanical components, all enclosed within the machine’s cabinet to provide a sturdy, safe, and clean polishing process:
The polishing section of the machine is comprised of the polish table and associated mechanical support hardware.
The cassette wafer handling assembly is designed to provide a safe and convenient method for robotic loading and unloading of wafers.
--[p366]-- MECHANICAL COMPONENTS
The machine consists of three major mechanical components, all enclosed within the machine’s cabinet to provide a sturdy, safe, and clean polishing process:
The polishing section of the machine is comprised of the polish table and associated mechanical support hardware.
The cassette wafer handling assembly is designed to provide a safe and convenient method for robotic loading and unloading of wafers.
--[p366]-- In addition, the bridge provides the oscillatory motion of the spindle drives during wafer polishing upon the polish table. Together the rigid bridge structure and smooth oscillatory motion of the spindle drives produce wafer surface uniformity and maximize polish table pad life.
--[p28]-- Mechanical, electrical, and software interlocks provide for user safety during all machine operations.
The bridge assembly, a rigid structure containing the spindle drive assemblies and their support hardware, travels on ball bearing slides to supply smooth, accurate horizontal motion of the spindle drive assemblies. The bridge traverses from the (primary) polish table to the load stations or the optional second table to facilitate transfer of wafers in process through the machine.

===== [p233-233] CONDITIONING/CLEANINGPARAMETERS MENU(SCREEN PAGE 2) > "SINGLE" SWEEP STYLE CHOICE: (1块) =====
--[p233]-- "SINGLE" SWEEP STYLE CHOICE:
The choice Single is among the One way and Two way sweep style choices in the Conditioning/Cleaning Menu. If Single is selected, the value in the Conditioning Cycles choice will specify a number of single sweep traverses. For example, if Conditioning Cycles is set to "3" and Sweep Start is set to Outer, the arm swill sweep three times (out to in, in to out, and out to in).

===== [p482-482] PLUMBING DESCRIPTION COMPRESSED AIR SYSTEM > VACUUM SYSTEM (3块) =====
--[p482]-- VACUUM SYSTEM
The vacuum system controls the vacuum source needed to secure the wafer carriers to the spindle drives, the wafer to the robot end effector, and the wafers to the load chucks. Vacuum (back pressure) also pulls the wafers up off the load chucks and into the carriers. The inhouse vacuum source must be a minimum of 25 inches Hg. Each of the five vacuum lines has a control valve mounted on the solenoid panel.
--[p482]-- Two back pressure vacuum regulators control vacuum and air pressure to the wafer in the carrier.
Normally open valves are used on the spindles; thus, if the machine loses power, the wafer carriers will not fall off the spindle drive assemblies. When the solenoid of either of the spindle valves is de-energized, air pilot pressure forces the valve's diaphragm down to divert vacuum to the cylinder port. Air pilot pressure must be available to permit the diaphragm to move.
--[p482]-- When the solenoid is energized, the air pilot source is cut off, allowing the spring to return the diaphragm and close off the vacuum source. Vacuum switches on each line test to see if vacuum is in the line, indicating that a wafer carrier is attached. Whenever a solenoid is de-energized to release a wafer carrier, the blow-off solenoid energizes, routing air into the vacuum lines to release the grip upon the wafer carrier.

===== [p29-367] ABOUT THE MODEL 6DS-SP PLANARIZER > ELECTRICAL DISTRIBUTION AND CONTROL (8块) =====
--[p29]-- ELECTRICAL DISTRIBUTION AND CONTROL
The Model 6DS-SP Planarizer’s electrical distribution and control systems are designed to provide all necessary control functions for polish process optimization while maintaining the reliability and ease of use necessary for the production environment.
The focus of the control system is the control computer, an IBM Industrial PC personal computer, supplying maximum reliability and functionality in an industry standard package.
--[p29]-- A flat panel display, keypad, and keyboard interface the planarizer with the user through menu-oriented commands shown on the display. The flat panel display, keypad, keyboard, and control panel form a user interface unit that is mounted on the left front of the machine cabinet on a fully-adjustable support arm. Dual front and side interfaces and a mobile remote interface are available as options.
--[p29]-- In addition to the control computer and interface hardware, the control system includes an industry standard input/output (I/O) system. A second computer board resides in the control computer for dedicated control of six or more of the planarizer's servo motor axes, with a third computer board controlling the other eight servo motor axes. Together the I/O, servo controllers, and control computer maintain communication for complete control of all machine functions.
--[p29]-- The planarizer design takes advantage of such benefits inherent in the application of a personal computer for process control as widespread hardware availability and support, understanding of PC operation among users and engineers, and very cost effective performance due to large scale production of PC's for factory applications.
The 6DS-SP uses a standard "off the shelf" computer package rather than a customized card cage to maintain simplicity, reliability, and economy.

===== [p467-467] DC MOTOR CONTROLLER > SERVO AMPLIFIER (4块) =====
--[p467]-- Whenever the fault line voltage is high, the motor contactor is disabled, and all power to that DC servo motor is cut off.
The amplifier module receives an analog velocity command signal from the servo module of the motion control board. In response to the velocity command input, the amplifier module uses pulse width modulation (PWM) for exciting the motor windings, to ramp the motor up or down to constant velocity.
--[p467]-- The axis 1- 4 encoder emulator, mounted on the amplifier module, translates the resolver feedback signals from the motor into the encoder signals required by the motion controller system. These signals provide data on the motor's absolute position and velocity.
--[p467]-- The axes 1-4 amplifier modules are supplied with three phase 208 VAC, and wired to the motor's windings through a motor contactor. The motor contactor is enabled when the fault line output of the amplifier module is low. This low output energizes an inline relay coil which in turn closes its contacts to energize the motor contactor coil, completing the power source path to the DC servo motor.
--[p467]-- SERVO AMPLIFIER
Refer to engineering drawings 217946E2 through 217946E9 and 217946EA through 217946EE for the following discussion. For each of the motors discussed above in the Servo Controller section, an amplifier module mates between the motion control board and the brushless DC servo motor. The amplifier modules are identified as 1BSC through 12BSC for axes 1 through 12 respectively.

===== [p98-98] CONFIRMING THAT UTILITY SOURCES MEET REQUIREMENTS > TEMPERATURE-CONTROLLED WATER (2块) =====
--[p98]-- A bypass valve, coolant bypass (11A), mounted at the rear of the machine, provides overpressure protection for the polish table. If coolant back pressure rises above 10 PSI, the coolant bypass valve opens and dumps to the table drain (8) to prevent damage to the table.
--[p98]-- TEMPERATURE-CONTROLLED WATER
The coolant in (11) and coolant out (6) permit the cycling of temperaturecontrolled water through the polish table for a temperature-controlled polishing process. Both connections require mating to the machine's 3/4-inch PVC threaded pipe joints. The pressure regulator adjusts the pressure of the liquid flowing through the loop. The coolant in (11) and coolant out (6) must be connected to the temperature control unit.

===== [p232-232] CONDITIONING/CLEANINGPARAMETERS MENU(SCREEN PAGE 2) > IN-SITU CONDITIONING DUTY CYCLE: (1块) =====
--[p232]-- IN-SITU CONDITIONING DUTY CYCLE:
The percentage of time conditioning occurs during polishing can be set with the In-situ Duty Cycle value in the Conditioning/Cleaning Parameters Menu. The arm is raised and conditioning is paused the required time after each complete 2 way sweep to effect the duty cycle. If the duty cycle is set to 100%, in-situ conditioning will be continuous. If set to 0%, there will be one 2 way sweep after which the arm will raise and pause indefinitely.
(In -situ conditioning always starts when polishing starts.)

===== [p486-487] PLUMBING DESCRIPTION COMPRESSED AIR SYSTEM > DRAIN SYSTEM (4块) =====
--[p487]-- The drain tub for the polish table assembly is equipped with a rinse ring consisting of several spray nozzles mounted around the pan to thoroughly rinse the bottom of the pan. During the auto polish cycle, rinse water from the rinse ring spurts at fixed time intervals, keeping the bottom of the tub relatively clean and preventing the slurry solution from clogging up the drainpipe.
--[p486]-- DRAIN SYSTEM
The drain system consists of drain tubs (surrounding the elevator assembly , the shuttle assembly, and the polish table assembly) and hoses for exporting the collected waste fluids. The elevator and shuttle drain tubs tie together and exit the machine. The polish table drain tub has a separate line.
The drain tubs are constructed of polypropylene for strength and resistance to damage from many types of fluids. The bottoms are inclined to collect waste fluids to a drainpipe.
--[p487]-- Three floor pans at the base of the machine catch drips or leaks and drain to a controlled site to prevent spillage onto the floor. With the drain pan alarm feature, each pan is equipped with a leak detect sensor to signal to the operator the existence of a leak in the machine as indicated by the presence of water in the pan.
This page intentionally left blank.
REVENTATIVE AINTENANCE CHEDULES
--[p486]-- Elevator and shuttle waste fluid is primarily D.I. water; polish table waste is primarily slurry solution. The drainpipe from each drain tub terminates at the bottom rear of the machine's back panel to separate connections. Each connection is a 1 1/2-inch threaded PVC pipe for joining to inhouse drain lines. The polish table drain has a cleanout port for clearing out debris.

--[p427]-- The elevator access doors must be closed to permit elevator and robot movements. If not, an automatic cycle may pause until the door is closed.
To open either polish section operator door requires pulling the latch assembly toward the operator and then pushing the door aside in its slider track. The Left Operator Door is latched closed by an air cylinder whenever the shuttle or second table assembly is in motion.

--[p430]-- 24 Main Power Supply Circuit Breaker
The Left and Right Electrical Cabinets both have service doors. These doors must be closed and latched before the machine can be powered up.
The Left Side Electrical Cabinet Service Door (19) must be completely closed to properly operate the door latch (23). The Rear Electrical Enclosure Latch (23) rotates counterclockwise to latch the service door and enable the Main Power Supply Circuit   
Breaker (24).
--[p425]-- OPERATOR DOOR INTERLOCKS
Opening a polish section operator door during a cycle interrupts and suspends the cycle. To continue the cycle, close the operator door and press the CYCLE START pushbutton on the control panel. If the cycle had been polishing, polishing will end but the rest of the cycle can be continued.
Opening an elevator access operator door will not halt the cycle, but it will prevent elevator and robot movements, pausing the cycle when those movements are required.
--[p428]-- 13 Elevator Access Doors
The Left Side Service Door (11) provides access to the front and side regulator and valve assembly panels. The regulator panels hold the regulators for adjusting the chuck and spindle blow off for left and right wafer carrier positions, load chuck raise pressure, and wafer blow off pressure as well as other functions.
Note: Wafer blow off pressure is used without a regulator on machines equipped with back pressure.
--[p431]-- The Right Side Service Doors (20) are secured by a key locked latch. To open the two right side service doors, rotate the latch. The Main Power Supply Circuit Breaker Lever (24) is thrown upward to enable power to the machine. The Rear Door Power On Lamp (22) will glow green to indicate power is on. The Rear Door Emergency Off Button (21) is provided for immediate stopping of all machine motion and turning off of control power.
--[p426]-- 6 Lower Left Front Service Door

--[p64]-- OPERATOR DOOR INTERLOCKS
Opening a polish section operator door during a cycle interrupts and suspends the cycle. To continue the cycle, close the operator door and press the CYCLE START pushbutton on the control panel. If the cycle had been polishing, polishing will end but the rest of the cycle can be continued.
Opening an elevator access operator door will not halt the cycle, but it will prevent elevator and robot movements, pausing the cycle when those movements are required.

1. Following procedures detailed in the Basic Operation section above, power up the machine and perform the home sequence routine.
Remove carriers from spindles:
2. Following procedures detailed above in this chapter, remove the carriers from spindles.
3. Place carriers on a work bench bottom side up.

4. Use a plastic scraper to raise one edge of pad.
5.
--[p173]-- Working from the previously placed portion of the pad, smooth the remaining pad into place.
14. Remove the alignment pins.
15. Use a plastic roller to help smooth out bubbles.
Note: If you can’t get the bubbles out, start over with a new pad. A quality product cannot be produced with a bubbled pad!
--[p173]-- Place a new pad on the carrier bottom (backing side down) and align its two notches with the alignment pins.
10. Peel back the backing two to three inches and fold it under (toward the center of the pad).
11. While continuing to maintain hole alignment, press the exposed adhesive portion of the pad down onto the carrier bottom.
12. Lift the backed portion of the pad and peel off the remaining backing.

b. Remove remaining residue with mild solvent.
c. Dry with soft cloth.

===== [p99-99] CONFIRMING THAT UTILITY SOURCES MEET REQUIREMENTS > DRAINS (3块) =====
--[p99]-- The second drain, labeled loader drain (9) is connected to the drain tub below the shuttle and elevators. With a standard machine configuration, this pipe carries D.I. water and residual amounts of slurry; thus, it may not require any special handling provisions. However, if a second polish table is installed, this drain may carry slurry, which requires a connection to a drain system designed for handling the disposal of such materials.
Both drain lines are 1-1/2" PVC pipe.
--[p99]-- Although the table drain pipe incorporates a cleanout branch inside the machine, an external cleanout is recommended for each drain pipe. Pipe unions are also recommended--located near each drain pipe connection to facilitate future pipe servicing or possible machine moving.
The slurry supply lines, slurry 1 supply (2) and slurry 2 supply (3), are described Slurry System Connection, below.
--[p99]-- DRAINS
Refer to the Safety section in Chapter One of this manual for further information on slurry compounds and waste disposal.
The Model 6DS-SP Planarizer has two drains, both clearly labeled and located at the rear. The drain connection for the polish table drain tub is labeled table drain (8). As mostly undiluted slurry will drain through the table drain pipe during polishing, this pipe should be connected to a drain system designed for handling the disposal of such materials.

===== [p45-383] APPENDIX TO LOCKOUT SAFETY PROCEDURE > Introduction (10块) =====
--[p45]-- The lockout device shall be used unless the employer can demonstrate that the utilization of a tagout system will provide full employee protection. The tagout device shall be non-reusable, attached by hand, self-locking, and non-releasing with a minimum unlocking strength of no less than 50 pounds and must be at least equivalent to an all-environment tolerant nylon cable tie.
--[p45]-- Introduction
On October 30, 1989, the Lockout/Tagout Standard, 29 CFR 1910.147, went into effect. It was created to help reduce the death and injury rate caused by the unexpected energization or startup of machines, or the release of stored energy. The standard covers the servicing and maintenance of machines and equipment in which the unexpected energization, start-up or release of stored energy could cause injury [29 CFR 1910.147 (a)(1)(i), 1910.147 (a)(2)(I)].
--[p383]-- The lockout device shall be used unless the employer can demonstrate that the utilization of a tagout system will provide full employee protection. The tagout device shall be non-reusable, attached by hand, self-locking, and non-releasing with a minimum unlocking strength of no less than 50 pounds and must be at least equivalent to an all-environment tolerant nylon cable tie.
--[p383]-- Normal production operations, cords and plugs under exclusive control, and hot tap operations are not covered [29 CPR 1910.147 (a)(2)(ii)]. This is intended to apply to energy sources such as electrical, mechanical, hydraulic, chemical, nuclear, and thermal.
--[p383]-- The lockout device must be substantial enough to prevent removal without use of excessive force or unusual techniques.
Tagout is the placement of a tagout device (a tag or other prominent warning device and a means of attachment) on an energy isolation device to indicate that the energy isolating device and the equipment being controlled may not be operated until the tagout device is removed.
--[p45]-- Lockout is the placement of a lockout device on an energy isolation device (circuit breaker, slide gate, line valve, disconnect switch, etc.) to ensure that the energy isolating device and equipment being controlled cannot be operated until the lockout device is removed. A lockout device utilizes a positive means such as a lock (key or combination type) to hold an energyisolating device in a safe position and prevent the energization of a machine or equipment.
--[p45]-- Normal production operations, cords and plugs under exclusive control, and hot tap operations are not covered [29 CPR 1910.147 (a)(2)(ii)]. This is intended to apply to energy sources such as electrical, mechanical, hydraulic, chemical, nuclear, and thermal.
--[p383]-- Lockout is the placement of a lockout device on an energy isolation device (circuit breaker, slide gate, line valve, disconnect switch, etc.) to ensure that the energy isolating device and equipment being controlled cannot be operated until the lockout device is removed. A lockout device utilizes a positive means such as a lock (key or combination type) to hold an energyisolating device in a safe position and prevent the energization of a machine or equipment.
--[p45]-- The lockout device must be substantial enough to prevent removal without use of excessive force or unusual techniques.
Tagout is the placement of a tagout device (a tag or other prominent warning device and a means of attachment) on an energy isolation device to indicate that the energy isolating device and the equipment being controlled may not be operated until the tagout device is removed.
--[p383]-- Introduction
On October 30, 1989, the Lockout/Tagout Standard, 29 CFR 1910.147, went into effect. It was created to help reduce the death and injury rate caused by the unexpected energization or startup of machines, or the release of stored energy. The standard covers the servicing and maintenance of machines and equipment in which the unexpected energization, start-up or release of stored energy could cause injury [29 CFR 1910.147 (a)(1)(i), 1910.147 (a)(2)(I)].

===== [p138-138] MENUS USED IN BASIC OPERATION > DUAL BACKPRESSURE CONTROL: (1块) =====
--[p138]-- DUAL BACKPRESSURE CONTROL:
Dual backpressure control permits setting the left and right backpressures in the Polish Parameter Menu to different values.
This feature permits compensation for process related left/right differences. It is not intended to mask other left/right differences due to machine miscalibration or carrier differences.

===== [p224-224] RECIPE MANAGEMENT MENU > Sweep Parameters Setup: (1块) =====
--[p224]-- Sweep Parameters Setup:
Determine the endpoints of the desired arm sweep in terms of the distance in inches from the table center to the center of the conditioning device. This will be influenced by wafer diameter, oscillation stroke, and conditioning device diameter.
In the Sweep Parameters Menu, enter these endpoints as the Outer and Inner values. The Outer value must be the larger of the two values.

===== [p74-75] CONTROL PANEL AND EMERGENCY OFF BUTTONS > CONTROL PANEL (6块) =====
--[p74]-- With the fixed or remote terminal option, an additional monitor (with keyboard) and control panel may be mounted above the elevators or on a mobile cart. Selection of the active keyboard is made at a switch located at the rear of the machine on the electrical cabinet.
The MACHINE ON lamp, to the left of the pushbutton, will indicate machine power-up was successful and the machine power is on.
--[p75]-- It may also indicate other trouble (such as a plugged drain pan). The alarm accompanies the error message displayed on the monitor. Alarm parameters are discussed in detail in the Machine Setup chapter of the 6DS-SP Operations manual.
--[p75]-- To restart after correcting the problem requiring the emergency off, close the service door, and follow the procedures in the Operator Functions chapter of the 6DS-SP Operations manual for powering up the machine, homing, and running an auto cycle.
The AUDIBLE ALARM is located on the control panel at the bottom row and left of the EMERG OFF pushbutton. It sounds whenever a machine parameter exceeds a programmed range of values during polishing.
--[p74]-- CONTROL PANEL
Note: Cabinet configurations vary to accommodate customized features, and some control panel components may be placed elsewhere. A component’s function remains the same regardless of its location.
The control panel is located on the Model 6DS-SP Planarizer at the top center front of the machine. Figure 2-6 shows the layout of the panel components. A description of each component follows the figure.
--[p75]-- The CYCLE START pushbutton starts machine operations from the Machine Operations/Shutdown Menus selections, as described in the Operator Functions chapter of the 6DS-SP Operations manual.
The CYCLE HALT pushbutton halts the selected cycle before its completion, suspending machine action. Press the CYCLE START pushbutton to continue the cycle.
--[p75]-- The EMERG OFF pushbutton is an emergency off button; when pressed it instantly stops all machine motion and turns off power to all subassemblies and controllers.
After pressing an EMERG OFF button, the operator restarts the machine from the beginning by pressing the MACHINE ON pushbutton.

===== [p412-413] STEP 5 - CONFIRMING THAT UTILITY SOURCES MEET REQUIREMENTS > EXHAUST FAILURE INDICATOR (3块) =====
--[p413]-- If available, install the Exhaust Failure Monitoring system by connecting the Exhaust Failure cable to the appropriate 4-pin AMP receptacle on the bottom of the large electrical cabinet
--[p412]-- EXHAUST FAILURE INDICATOR
The 6DS-SP offers a system to relay a signal from the machine operator’s facility exhaust failure monitoring system to the local 6DS-SP machine operator. The system requires the user to supply a safety-rated normally-open contact or switch. Closing of that contact, if connected to the 6DS-SP machine, will "announce" an exhaust failure by turning on a set of red lamps, sounding intermittent 85 dB audible alarms, and displaying an alarm message on the screen.
--[p412]-- If the GEM option is installed, the machine will also communicate the exhaust failure to the host computer.
• Above Elevator Doors (left side of machine)
• Above Front Polish Doors (front of machine)
The interface connection for the exhaust failure alarm system is located on the bottom of the large electrical cabinet on the rear of the machine.

===== [p47-385] GALLIUM ARSENIDE AND GERMANIUM USE > GALLIUM ARSENIDE (GAAS) (2块) =====
--[p385]-- GALLIUM ARSENIDE (GAAS)
Gallium arsenide is used in the semiconductor industry in the form of polished wafers with a dark gray metallic sheen.
Gallium arsenide technology (GaAs) III-V binary compound possesses good electrical properties, making this material highly attractive for electronic applications. In addition, GaAs possesses good and unique optoelectronic properties because it can be prepared in a semi-insulating state or behavior.
\- Electronic Materials Handbook, ASM International, Vol.
1, pp. 199.

===== [p42-380] LOCKOUT SAFETY PROCEDURE > PREPARATION FOR LOCKOUT (2块) =====
--[p380]-- PREPARATION FOR LOCKOUT
Maintenance personnel authorized to perform lockout shall be certain as to which switch, valve or other energy isolating devices apply to the equipment being locked out. More than one energy source (electrical, mechanical, or others) may be involved. Any questionable identification of sources shall be cleared by the employees with their supervisors. Before lockout commences, job authorization should be obtained.

===== [p118-118] CALIBRATION/CONFIGURATION CHANGES (1块) =====
--[p118]-- CALIBRATION/CONFIGURATION CHANGES
Reflecting a reorganization of the handling of calibration and configuration choices, the Calibration/Configuration Menu of Version 4.25 and later contains only technician level calibration variables and one-time machine configuration that would not be changed by an operator or engineer.

--[p234]-- MACHINE PARAMETERS MENU(SCREEN PAGE 1 )
This menu/page permits setting the most commonly changed parameters for machine operation. (The other two screen pages for this menu contain parameters that are seldom changed.) These parameters can affect process and are therefore saved as part of the recipe. (Other machine settings can be found in the Machine Parameters and Calibration/Configuration menus.)
The Spindle Force Mode can be set for either constant pressure or constant temperature.
--[p234]-- In the constant pressure mode, the polish force will be whatever is entered in the Polish Parameters Menu. In the constant temperature mode, force will be varied to attempt to maintain the pad temperature to the value entered in Pad Temperature. If the constant pressure mode is used, the Pad Temperature value is ignored.
The Left Force Scaling and Right Force Scaling values will cause the actual polish force to differ from the polish parameter force by the percent entered.
--[p234 [表]]-- This is intended to compensate for left/right polish differences that are process related. They should not be used to compensate for differences that are due to miscalibration of the machine.

===== [p53-391] GALLIUM ARSENIDE AND GERMANIUM USE > REACTIVITY WARNINGS (2块) =====
--[p391]-- REACTIVITY WARNINGS
When heated, germanium is incompatible with bromine, chlorine, fluorine, oxygen, potassium chloride, and potassium. Additionally, mixing with aqua regia, concentrated nitric or sulfuric acids, fused alkalies, nitrates or carbonates, halogens, and oxidants should be avoided. When germanium decomposes, germanium dioxide is formed.
--[p53]-- REACTIVITY WARNINGS

===== [p131-131] MENUS USED IN BASIC OPERATION > WARNING: (2块) =====
--[p131]-- The section below provides details on selection available at the menus used in basic machine operation.
For step-by-step procedures for using the menus, refer to the Basic Operation section of this chapter.
--[p131]-- WARNING:
DO NOT OPERATE A 6DS-SP WITH AN UNLOADED CARRIER IN THE MACHINE!
A carrier which is loaded on a spindle may not clear an unloaded carrier sitting on a load or cleaning station.
During bridge and shuttle moves, loaded carriers can collide with unloaded carriers, causing machine damage.
Therefore, always remove loose carriers from the machine before taking any action that will cause machine motions.

===== [p139-139] MENUS USED IN BASIC OPERATION > “ON THE FLY” CHANGES: (2块) =====
--[p139]-- “ON THE FLY” CHANGES:
Numerous recipe parameter changes may be made while the machine is operating.
For example, past, present, or future polishing steps can be changed. If the current step's time is changed to a longer time than what has transpired, the remaining time showing will increase by the same amount as the increase. If the current step's time is shorter than what has transpired, the step will end.
Many conditioning and machine parameters may be changed.
--[p139]-- However, changes that could cause trouble, such as changing the number of spindles used, will be ignored until the start of the next cycle.
Finally, all polish alarm parameters can be changed in the Alarms Menu.

===== [p475-475] POWER DISTRIBUTION > INTERLOCKS (3块) =====
--[p475]-- INTERLOCKS
There are six interlock switches for the machine's seven service doors. Each service door has its own switch except for the left electrical cabinet service door. The interlock switch used is a double acting spring loaded switch. When the service door is in place, the switch plunger is depressed, and the contact is closed. When the door is out of position, the switch contact is open.
--[p475]-- For machines with the Mobile Remote Unit option (SA 219187), the following CAUTION applies:
During the temporary thirty (30) second bypass of the Mobile Remote E.M.O. circuit, the Mobile Remote Unit E.M.O. button WILL NOT BE OPERABLE! However, all other machine E.M.O. buttons WILL remain operable.
ÀDANGER
HAZARDOUS VOLTAGE CAN CAUSE SEVERE INJURY OR DEATH
Service in this area must be performed by authorized personnel only
--[p475]-- The switch contact can only be closed without the door present by pulling the switch plunger forward until the spring is out of the plunger's detent and the switch contacts are closed.
The six interlock switches and the Emergency Off pushbuttons (EMO’s) are wired together in series. The EMO’s are normally closed, and the six interlock switches are wired as normally open. Four or more EMO’s are installed on the machine, depending upon customer requirements.

===== [p468-468] I/O AND INTERFACE SYSTEM (5块) =====
--[p468]-- I/O AND INTERFACE SYSTEM
The I/O and interface system hardware used in the machine form an industrial standard optically isolated I/O system. This system incorporates brain boards, driver modules, and a host computer interface card to read or drive all digital and analog signals. Digital inputs and outputs are of one of two possible voltage levels, either zero volts or +24 volts, to represent a device condition as either "on" or "off".
--[p468]-- Digital outputs are used to turn on or off solenoids and relays throughout the machine. Digital inputs monitor such switches and sensors as the control panel pushbuttons and bridge limit switches. Analog inputs and outputs are used for devices that have a range of values represented by varying voltage or current levels (for example, the spindle force load cells, the slurry pH transmitters, and the DC motor drive boards).
--[p468]-- They are identified as the Digital I/O Mounting Racks 1MR, 2MR, 3MR, and 4MR, the 8 Analog I/O Mounting Rack, and the 16 Analog I/O Mounting Rack. Each I/O mounting rack has a brain board. The I/O mounting racks hold the individual I/O driver modules; several types of driver modules are used on the racks. The modules are individually listed and identified with accompanying part numbers on engineering drawing 217946EM.
--[p468]-- All six I/O mounting racks and the interface adapter card inside the control computer are chained together with a single 50 conductor ribbon cable, establishing a communication bus line between all I/O mounting racks and the control computer. The control computer makes all software decisions and provides instructions concerning the individual I/O points. The brain boards of the six mounting racks implement the instructions.
--[p468]-- A high speed interface adapter card resides in one expansion slot of the control computer, interfacing the computer motherboard to the I/O bus and conveying input and output instructions from the control computer for specific I/O points. As shown in engineering drawing 217946EM, six I/O racks are mounted on the machine back panel located inside the right side electrical cabinet.

===== [p51-389] GALLIUM ARSENIDE AND GERMANIUM USE > GERMANIUM (GE) (2块) =====
--[p389]-- GERMANIUM (GE)
Germanium is used in the semiconductor industry in the form of polished wafers.
Germanium crystals are grown in rods up to 1-3/8 in. (3.49 cm) in diameter for use in making transistor wafers. High-purity crystals are used for both P and N semiconductors. They are easier to purify and have a lower melting point than other semiconductors, specifically silicon.
\- Electronic Materials Handbook, ASM International, Vol. 1, pp. 393.
--[p51]-- GERMANIUM (GE)

===== [p138-138] MENUS USED IN BASIC OPERATION > ODD WAFER POLISHING: (3块) =====
--[p138]-- The Stat display will show Odd Wafer Polish when polishing begins. When polishing is finished, the machine will automatically return to normal polishing and either continue, if more wafers had been presented to the machine, or stop if the machine still has no more wafers.
The Odd Wafer Time Adjust can be used to lengthen or shorten the polish times for the odd wafer polish cycle. All times for both tables will be multiplied by this value which is entered as a percent.
The nominal value of 100 % will cause no change to polish times. During odd wafer polishing, the adjusted times will show on the Auto Polish Menu.
--[p138]-- ODD WAFER POLISHING:
This feature permits a machine set for dual spindle polishing to polish a single remaining (odd) wafer. This feature is applicable in the automatic (cassette to cassette) mode only.
Odd Wafer Polish and Odd Wafer Time Adjust choices are available in the Machine Parameters Menu.
If Odd Wafer Polish is disabled, this feature will not be used.
--[p138]-- If an odd wafer situation occurs, the machine will stall and wait for another wafer after loading the odd wafer on the left load station.
If Odd Wafer Polish is enabled, the machine will attempt to normally place a wafer first on the left load station and then on the right for every polish cycle. If, after placing a wafer on the left load station, no more wafers can be found, the machine will polish the odd wafer using the left spindle only.

===== [p171-171] POLISHING PAD REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION > Installation (2块) =====
--[p171]-- Use a plastic roller to help smooth out bubbles.
Note: If you can’t get the bubbles out, start over with a new pad. A quality product cannot be produced with a bubbled pad!
--[p171]-- Installation
Install the new pad:
1. Place a new pad on the clean table (backing side down) and center it.
2. Peel back the backing three to four inches and fold it under (toward the center of the pad).
3. While continuing to maintain alignment, press the exposed adhesive portion of the pad down onto the table.
Lift the backed portion of the pad and peel off the remaining backing.
5. Working from the previously placed portion of the pad, smooth the remaining pad into place.

===== [p473-473] POWER DISTRIBUTION > DC DISTRIBUTION (2块) =====
--[p473]-- DC DISTRIBUTION
The DC voltage distribution consists of three individual power supplies, 1PS for 24 VDC, 2PS for +/- 15 VDC, and 3PS for 5 VDC, and their respective terminal blocks, 3TS, 4TS, and 5TS. Each DC power supply has its terminal strip to branch out DC power throughout the machine as shown in the remaining electrical schematics.
Power supply 1PS sources 24 VDC power for inputs and outputs on the Digital I/O Racks 1MR, 2MR, 3MR, and 4MR.
--[p473]-- These outputs enable relays 1CR through 32CR and solenoid valves for pneumatic, vacuum, and water lines. Power supply 2PS sources +/- 15 VDC power for all the analog inputs and outputs found on the Analog I/O Racks. Power supply 3PS provides +5 VDC to the Digital I/O Racks 1MR, 2MR, 3MR, and 4MR and the two Analog I/O Racks to power their internal circuitry.

===== [p467-467] DC MOTOR CONTROLLER (2块) =====
--[p467]-- The conditioning brush rotate drive motor operates at a constant speed. The motor speed adjustment for the brush's rotational speed is a potentiometer mounted below its control board. The velocity profile for each control board is adjusted by several potentiometers on the board.
--[p467]-- DC MOTOR CONTROLLER
The 6DS-SP has five DC drive motors driven by complete control boards. Each controller receives an analog voltage input and drives the 90 VDC motor to a corresponding velocity. The five DC drive motors power the slurry 1, slurry 2, pump 3, conditioning brush sweep, and conditioning brush rotate functions. The first four receive an analog input command for motor speed from the control computer through the I/O interface system, respectively, channels 14, 15, 16, and 24.

--[p221 [表]]-- Each step has a corresponding time and force. By varying the times and/or forces, any linear or non-linear sweep behavior can be generated.
The Times = 1st and Forces = 1st function keys can be used to avoid tedious repetitive number entry if all times or all forces will be the same. --[p221]-- SWEEP PARAMETERS MENU
This menu permits setting parameters that determine how the programmable conditioning arm will sweep across the table. (The Conditioning/Cleaning Parameters Menu has other conditioning choices.) If the programmable arm is not installed, the Sweep Parameters Menu will not display.
The sweep range extends from the "outer" to the "inner" position. This range is divided into 20 segments. Segment l is at the outer position, and segment 20 is at the inner position.

===== [p184-184] CYCLE HALTING FUNCTIONS AND ASSOCIATED PROCEDURES > Notes: (2块) =====
--[p184]-- Opening an elevator area operator door during an auto polish cycle does not interrupt polishing, but it does suspend elevator movement and robot movement in the elevator area.
The auto cycle will resume after a halt regardless of the point in the cycle at which the halt occurred.
--[p184]-- Notes:
Opening a service door at any time shuts power down to the entire machine, including the control computer.
Opening a polish area operator door during an auto polish cycle interrupts and suspends the cycle. If a front (polish area) operator door is opened during an auto cycle, all machine functions, including bridge operation, will be suspended. The cycle will resume when the door is again closed.

===== [p436-436] CONTROL PANEL AND EMERGENCY OFF BUTTONS > Audible Alarm (1块) =====
--[p436]-- Audible Alarm
The AUDIBLE ALARM is mounted on the left side of the operator interface unit, adjacent to the control panel. It sounds whenever a machine parameter exceeds a programmed range of values during polishing. It may also indicate other trouble (such as a plugged drain pan). The alarm accompanies the error message displayed on the monitor. Alarm parameters are discussed in detail in the Machine Setup chapter of the 6DS-SP Operations manual.

===== [p105-105] AUTO POLISH CYCLEOPERATION - THE SEQUENCEOF EVENTS > D. WAFER UNLOADING SEQUENCE (1块) =====
--[p105]-- D. WAFER UNLOADING SEQUENCE
1. A test is done to make sure wafer(s) are on spindle(s).
2. The bridge moves to its load position.
3. If wafer cleaning is enabled:
a. The shuttle moves back.
b. The spindles move down into the cleaning stations.
c. The spindles rotate according to the wafer cleaning parameters set.
d. When wafer cleaning is finished, the spindles rise.
e. The shuttle moves forward.
f. The spindles move down to the load stations.

===== [p170-171] POLISHING PAD REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION > Removal (2块) =====
--[p170]-- Removal
Turn machine power ON and perform home sequence:
1. Following procedures detailed above, power up the machine and perform the home sequence routine.
Remove table pad and clean table:
2. Open the Right Side Operator Door.
3. Swing the slurry tubes to the rear of the machine.
4. Lift and remove the white plastic splash ring from the table.
5. Use a plastic scraper to raise one edge of the pad.
6. Peel the pad off by rolling to the opposite edge.
7. Discard the used pad.
8.
--[p171]-- Clean and dry the table with a soft cloth:
a. Feel the table by hand for adhesive residue.
b. Remove remaining residue with mild solvent.
c. Dry with soft cloth.

===== [p442-442] FLAT PANEL DISPLAY OPERATOR INTERFACE,KEYPAD, AND KEYBOARD > Calibration/Configuration Menu (1块) =====

Values involved in machine calibration and configuration are entered at this menu. Calibration refers to adjustments made by technicians (such as servo positions, force scale factors, etc.). ===== [p207-207] MACHINE SETUP > “ON THE FLY” RECIPE PARAMETER CHANGES (2块) =====
--[p207]-- However, changes that could cause trouble, such as changing the number of spindles used, will be ignored until the start of the next cycle.
Finally, all polish alarm parameters can be changed in the Alarms Menu.
--[p207]-- “ON THE FLY” RECIPE PARAMETER CHANGES
A number recipe parameter changes may now be made while the machine is operating.
For example, past, present, or future polishing steps can be changed. If the current step's time is changed to a longer time than what has transpired, the remaining time showing will increase by the same amount as the increase. If the current step's time is shorter than what has transpired, the step will end.
Many conditioning and machine parameters may be changed.

===== [p78-78] CONTROL COMPUTER > KEYBOARDS (1块) =====
--[p78]-- KEYBOARDS
Two keyboards are available with the 6DS-SP, a flat panel mounted on the bezel of the monitor or a PC (personal computer) style enhanced keyboard. Either keyboard cable plugs into the extender cable connection centrally located on top of the machine cabinet. Only one of the two keyboards can operate at a time.
To switch keyboards, shut the machine power OFF, plug in the desired keyboard, and then power UP again.
For details on use of the keyboards, refer to the Operator Functions chapter of the 6DS-SP Operations manual.

===== [p483-483] PLUMBING DESCRIPTION COMPRESSED AIR SYSTEM > EXHAUST SYSTEM (2块) =====
--[p483]-- EXHAUST SYSTEM
The exhaust system consists of hoses, a fixture surrounding the base of the polish table, and connection to an inhouse exhaust source. The exhaust system prevents the build up of vapors during the polishing process from the slurry solution and traps and exhausts airborne particles from the polishing process. A six-inch collar at the rear of the machine connects to the inhouse exhaust source.
--[p483]-- The exhaust system also collects the exhaust from all the solenoid valves used on the pneumatic, air pilot and compressed air lines, preventing individual solenoids from blowing port exhaust into the surrounding atmosphere. The exhaust ports from the solenoid valves are plumbed to a collection manifold and then to the six-inch duct of the exhaust system to exit through the inhouse exhaust source.

===== [p450-450] MECHANICAL DESCRIPTION > E. CASSETTE REMOVAL (1块) =====
--[p450]-- E. CASSETTE REMOVAL
The operator:
1. opens the elevator doors.
2. raises the elevator cassette sensor arm.
3. closes the elevator doors and waits for the elevators to rise to slot 26.
4. removes the cassette of processed wafers from the receive elevator.

===== [p402-402] STEP 2 - UNPACKING AND INSPECTION > LEVELING REQUIREMENT (1块) =====
--[p402]-- LEVELING REQUIREMENT
The Model 6DS-SP Planarizer must be level for proper operation.
Using the polish table surface as a reference plane, level the machine to within 0.010 inches per foot.
Leveling the polish table will optimize the machine position for even distribution of slurry solution on the polish table surface.

===== [p274-428] FREQUENTLY ENCOUNTERED PROBLEM CONDITIONS > \* Notes on Opening Doors: (2块) =====
--[p274]-- \* Notes on Opening Doors:
Opening a service door at any time shuts power down to the entire machine, including the control computer.
Opening a polish area operator door during an auto polish cycle interrupts and suspends the cycle.
Opening an elevator area operator door during an auto polish cycle does not interrupt polishing, but it does suspend elevator movement and robot movement.
--[p428]-- \* Notes on Opening Doors:
Opening a service door at any time shuts power down to the entire machine, including the control computer.
Opening a polish area operator door during an auto polish cycle interrupts and suspends the cycle.
Opening an elevator area operator door during an auto polish cycle does not interrupt polishing, but it does suspend elevator movement and robot movement.

===== [p129-129] CALIBRATION/CONFIGURATION CHANGES > New Feature at All Menus - “Menu “Hopping” (1块) =====
--[p129]-- New Feature at All Menus - “Menu “Hopping”
Menu "hopping" (menu changing) is permitted while the machine is operating. While all menus are always accessible, some function key choices may be "ghosted" if the choices would conflict with the current machine operation. (There is no longer any "Main Menu".)
Menu "hopping" permits viewing setups, viewing diagnostics, and making some "on the fly" changes concurrent with machine operation.

===== [p97-97] CONFIRMING THAT UTILITY SOURCES MEET REQUIREMENTS > VACUUM AND D.I. WATER (1块) =====
--[p97]-- VACUUM AND D.I. WATER
The connections for vacuum (5), D.I. water (10), and D. I. water return (10a) are located near the center of the machine cabinet and clearly labeled.
A bulkhead fitting is provided for each system to be connected to flexible tubing. The tubing should be selected to provide the necessary flow and pressure for the machine.

===== [p248-248] ADDITIONAL FEATURES AT THE MACHINE PARAMETERS MENU > SLURRY ALARM ACTION CHOICE: (1块) =====
--[p248]-- SLURRY ALARM ACTION CHOICE:
Calibration variable 59 "Slry alrm action (0-no, l-yes)" permits assignment of certain action to the presence of an alarm indicating low or absent slurry.
If set to "0", slurry alarms will display as information only.
If set to " 1 ", cycle starting will be inhibited if any polish step requires a slurry that has an alarm. If already in an auto cycle, a "finish cycle" will be automatically set if such an alarm occurs.
Finally, if not in a cycle the alarm will still display as information only.

===== [p124-124] CALIBRATION/CONFIGURATION CHANGES > Keypad (shown in Figure 3-3) (1块) =====
--[p124]-- Keypad (shown in Figure 3-3)
All letters are upper case only.
The function of the Shift key differs from the Shift on a standard keyboard. Characters in the upper right corner of a key are obtained by pressing the Shift key and the key of choice at the same time.
The Ctrl and Alt keys are functionally identical to those found on a standard keyboard.

===== [p146-146] MENUS USED IN BASIC OPERATION > DO NOT OPERATE A 6DS-SP WITH AN UNLOADED CARRIER IN THE MACHINE! (1块) =====
--[p146]-- DO NOT OPERATE A 6DS-SP WITH AN UNLOADED CARRIER IN THE MACHINE!
A carrier which is loaded on a spindle may not clear an unloaded carrier sitting on a load or cleaning station.
During bridge and shuttle moves, loaded carriers can collide with unloaded carriers, causing machine damage.
Therefore, always remove loose carriers from the machine before taking any action that will cause machine motions.

Note: To set or confirm recipe parameters, follow the procedures found in the Machine Setup chapter of this manual referring to the Conditioning/Cleaning Parameters Menu.

===== [p400-400] STEP 2 - UNPACKING AND INSPECTION (1块) =====
--[p400]-- STEP 2 - UNPACKING AND INSPECTION
The Model 6DS-SP Planarizer is shipped from the factory vacuum sealed (to prevent contamination during shipping) and fastened to a shipping pallet. Before unpacking the machine from its shipping provisions, inspect the exterior carefully for any indication of possible shipping damage. If such signs exist, contact the shipper to report a claim and obtain additional instructions before proceeding.

===== [p106-106] AUTO POLISH CYCLEOPERATION - THE SEQUENCEOF EVENTS > E. CASSETTE REMOVAL (1块) =====
--[p106]-- E. CASSETTE REMOVAL
The operator:
1. opens the elevator doors.
2. raises the elevator cassette sensor arm.
3. closes the elevator doors and waits for the elevators to rise to slot 26.
4. removes the cassette of processed wafers from the receive elevator.

===== [p436-436] CONTROL PANEL AND EMERGENCY OFF BUTTONS > Emergency Off (2块) =====
--[p436]-- Emergency Off
The red EMERGENCY OFF pushbutton is one of several emergency off buttons placed on the machine; when pressed it instantly stops all machine motion and turns off power to all subassemblies and controllers.
After pressing an EMERGENCY OFF button, the operator restarts the machine from the beginning by pressing the MACHINE ON pushbutton.
--[p436]-- To restart after correcting the problem requiring the emergency off, close all machine doors, and follow the procedures in the Operator Functions chapter of the 6DS-SP Operations manual for powering up the machine, homing, and running an auto cycle.

Software version 4.14 (July 14, 1995) adds two features:
Settable spindle flush water and air blow off times.
Two table machine wafer cleaning and/or carrier pad cleaning.

===== [p460-460] 6DS-SP VERSION 4.14 NEW FEATURES / INSTALLATION > Settable Spindle Flush Water and Air Blowoff Times: (4块) =====
--[p460]-- Settable Spindle Flush Water and Air Blowoff Times:
Calibration variable 176 "Flush water time (secs)" Calibration variable 177 "Flush air blowout time (secs)"
Calibration variables 176 and 177 permit setting the times for water and air blowoff during automatic cycle spindle flushing. These can be used with the existing calibration variable 173 "Approx flush blowout pres(psi)" to customize flushing for a specific application.
--[p460]-- (The forced spindle flush available in the Auto Polish menu does not use these times and instead uses "hard coded" times for a roughly 1 minute flush cycle.)
Typically the water time should be very short and the air blowoff time much longer. The original fixed times for the automatic cycle flush were 1 second for water and 12 seconds for air. To make the machine perform as it did originally, use these values.
--[p460]-- Also, the load rinse and, if the second table is installed, the carrier pad rinse will turn on during the entire flush cycle. Previously they were turned on during the last 2 seconds.
--[p460]-- Spindle flushing can be tested in the Diagnostics menu by forcing on flag 232 for the left spindle and flag 233 for the right spindle. During the water flush time, a "slug" of water will be introduced into the backpressure line. During the subsequent air blowoff time, that slug of water should be pushed through the line and out the carrier. Once the water is out of the line and carrier, air will exit carrier pad holes confirming that the line is empty.

===== [p156-156] USER INTERFACE REFERENCE > MportRec (Import Recipe) Utility Program: (3块) =====
--[p156]-- · Prompt the operator to enter a new value if desired.
· Save the modified recipe file in a binary format that can be used by the 6DS-SP.
MportRec is 6DS-SP software version specific because recipe limit tests use data in the 6DS-SP software file RECLIMIT.DAT. The initial MportRec release is compatible with 6DS-SP software versions 4.33 and 4.34.
MportRec.Exe for 6DS-SP Version 4.33 Copyright 2000 by Strasbaugh, Inc. Ver 1.0

in a file format that can be used by the 6DS-SP.   
The saved recipe will have the file extension .REC.
To exit the program at any time press the Ctrl-C key combination.

--[p156]-- MportRec (Import Recipe) Utility Program:
MportRec imports a 6DS-SP recipe file from an Excel CSV format to the 6DS-SP file format so it can be used by the 6DS-SP. (This program is the companion to XportRec which exports 6DS-SP format recipe files to recipe files with the CSV format.)
MportRec will:
· Read a 6DS-SP CSV recipe file.
· Compare each recipe element against the limits established in RECLIMIT.DAT.
· Notify the operator of any out of limit recipe element.

===== [p410-411] 6DS-SP VERSION 4.18 NEW FEATURES / INSTALLATION > Force Cycling: (3块) =====
--[p410 [表]]-- Force Cycling:
Force cycling will reduce polish force to a minimum pressure for a period at an interval.   
Force cycling can be applied to only one polish step.
The Machine Parameters menu, page 4 shows the following choices:
Force Cycling | Enable/Disable
Force Cycling Step | 1
Force Cycling Interval | 0 | secs
Force Cycling Period | 0 | secs
During polishing, the Auto Polish Parameter menu force builds when the step starts.
--[p411]-- When the Force Cycling Interval time has passed, the force will be reduced to minimum for the Force Cycling Period time.
The minimum pressure will be the "pressure minimums" from calibration variables 32, 37, 42, and 47. Also, if backpressure is enabled it will be set to full vacuum during the force cycling step.
--[p411]-- (This helps prevent blowing the wafer off the carrier during the time of the reduced polish force.) If backpressure is disabled for the table, then the backpressure will remain disabled.

This menu permits storing, retrieving, and deleting recipes.
Recipes are shown sorted but only 75 can be shown at one time. If more than 75 exist, the indications "<MORE" or "MORE>" will show to indicate which direction (left or right) will show more. The "move" choices can be used to select any recipe.

===== [p261-261] 6DS-SP SOFTWARE VERSION 4.32 NEW FEATURES / INSTALLATION > "Keep Elevator Tanks Full" Feature: (6块) =====
--[p261]-- The following calibration variables control this feature:
Variable 226 "Keep elev tanks full (0-n, 1-y)"
Variable 227 "Elev tank purge off time(secs)"
Variable 228 "Elev tank purge on time (secs)"
If variable 226 is "0", the feature is disabled and elevator filling will be controlled by the time in variable 179 "Elev tank fill time (seconds)". Also, the drain valve will turn on for any tank with its cassette arm lifted. This is the standard fill and drain operation.
--[p261]-- If variable 226 is "1", the feature is enabled and the variable 179 time is not used. Each elevator tank's fill valve will be on continuously when the cassette arm is down.
If the cassette arm is up, the fill valve will be continuously off, continuously on, or cycling based on the times entered in variables 227 and 228. If cycling, the cycle starts with "off". Such cycling can periodically purge the tank and prevent bacteria growth.
--[p261]-- Alternatively, setting variable 226 to "0" will disable the feature and restore standard timed elevator tank filling which will turn off fill valves and turn on drain valves when cassette arms are up.
--[p261]-- "Keep Elevator Tanks Full" Feature:
Version 4.32 adds a feature to keep elevator tanks full in 6DS-SP's with pneumatically controlled fill and drain valves. Automatic draining does not occur with this feature so the tank will remain full. Also, this feature causes continuous flow into the tank whenever the cassette arm is down and causes optional cycled flow when the arm is up. Settable on and off times for the cycled flow permit setting a balance between purging the tank and water conservation.
--[p261 [表]]-- The following table shows the priority of how the arm and time choices control tank flow during cycling.
Cassette arm &quot;On&quot; time &quot;Off &quot; time Tank fill valve
Down | Ignored | Ignored | On continuously
Up | Zero | Ignored | Off continuously
Up | Non-zero | Zero | On continuously
Up | Non-zero | Non-zero | Cycles off and on
Note: Set calibration variable 178 "Elev water W/idle (0-no, 1-yes)" to "1" if you want water flow through the tanks when the machine is idle.
--[p261]-- Note: Any or all fill valves may be on at the same time. This will alter the water pressure available for flow to any one tank.
Note: For maintenance and tank cleaning, turning on the drain valves in the Diagnostic menu can drain tanks. However, once the Diagnostics Mode no longer exists, filling will continue based on the settings of the feature.
