===== [p232-232] IMPORTANT GENERAL INFORMATION > Additional Carrier Loading/Unloading Protective Shuttle Moves: (4块) =====
--[p232]-- Additional Carrier Loading/Unloading Protective Shuttle Moves:
Version 4.34 adds protective shuttle moves for all 6DS-SP configurations similar to the moves added in version 4.28 for F-B HTP configuration.
If the bridge is not already at the load stations, the shuttle will first move away from the bridge path, the bridge will move, and the shuttle will then be moved to a position under the spindles (unless using the "unload to table 2" feature).
--[p232]-- This helps protect against damage if a carrier is already loaded onto a spindle and a carrier is also sitting on a load station. Operators should not allow this to happen. But if it does, the resulting collision will occur with the weak force of the shuttle move compared to the strong force of the bridge move.
--[p232]-- They are rectangular plastic trays that hook onto the edge of the polish door opening and rest on the second table surface to permit sliding carriers to and from load stations. If not already in the proper positions, use the Manual Control menu to properly position the bridge and shuttle before placing the fixtures. Otherwise, if the bridge or shuttle is in the wrong position, the shuttle and table will move at the start of the carrier loading or unloading sequence.
--[p232]-- (When added in 4.28 for the F-B HTP configuration, in addition to carrier to carrier collision, this sequence also helped prevent damage if carriers with latches were improperly oriented or if gimbaled carriers were tilted too much.)
NOTE: Special instructions if using carrier loading fixtures (Strasbaugh part number 274559):
These fixtures are used only for two table configurations.

===== [p364-364] 6DS-SP SOFTWARE VERSION 4.23.1 NEW FEATURES / INSTALLATION > NOTES: (2块) =====
--[p364]-- NOTES:
During polishing, the total spindle force will be an amount equal to the desired polish force plus ring force. This total force will be distributed between the wafer and retaining ring such that the force applied to the wafer will be the desired polish force. The Frc display in the status area indicates wafer polish force.
The maximum force specification of the machine, 500 lbs, applies to total spindle force.
--[p364]-- The amount of that force that will actually be applied to the wafer will be reduced by the amount of the ring force.
If using fixed retaining rings, the Ring Force values in the Polish Parameters menu must be zero.
If using the "constant temperature" mode, polish force will be controlled to maintain a constant primary table pad temperature. Ring force is not specially controlled and will be whatever is in the recipe step regardless of temperature.

===== [p280-280] 6DS-SP SOFTWARE VERSION 4.31 NEW FEATURES / INSTALLATION > Carrier X Calibration Information for Technicians: (4块) =====
--[p280]-- Calibrate down force with units set for "lbs" and left and right force scaling set to 100%. The Manual Control menu requested spindle down force will be displayed as "Ring Frc" in the status display. "Ring Frc" always shows total spindle force minus membrane force. Therefore, the membrane force (shows as "Frc" in the status display) must display zero. With Manual Control membrane force disabled, these forces should be zero if they are properly calibrated.
--[p280]-- You can also enable membrane pressure, enter zero force, and the closed loop system should hold them at zero. If using psi, the ring force displayed will be converted based on calibration variable 207 "CarrX ring area (Sq in.)". You can force the status display ring force to show in terms of polish force if the actual wafer area is entered into variable 207. Also, the membrane offset value in calibration variable 208 "CarrX offset (lbs.)" does not matter for this calibration.
It would effect the membrane pressure if these are enabled, but not the overall spindle downforce.
--[p280]-- A nominal gain value of approximately "2" is a good starting point but a particular machine or application could easily require a different value.
Manual Control menu, page 3, will show membrane force choices. Calculations use calibration variables 206 and 208 as well as the left and right force scaling values exactly like polishing. Remember that the displayed forces are related to wafer polishing and are not the actual pressures within the carrier.
--[p280]-- Carrier X Calibration Information for Technicians:
Calibration Variable 57 "Back/membrane press cntrl gain" and variable 65 through 68, backpressure/membrane offset and scaling, are used for membrane pressure control since it is the same system otherwise used for backpressure. It is important that the control gain be high enough so that blowoff builds enough during the selected blowoff time. It is also important that the gain be low enough to prevent overshoot which can result in wafer slipouts.

===== [p368-369] 6DS-SP SOFTWARE VERSION 4.23.1 NEW FEATURES / INSTALLATION > New Light Tower Configuration: (3块) =====

===== [p343-343] 6DS-SP SOFTWARE VERSION 4.26.1 NEW FEATURES / INSTALLATION > Description of AGV > Polish> Cassette Mode: (1块) =====
--[p343]-- Description of AGV > Polish> Cassette Mode:
This is similar to the AGV > Polish > Scrubber mode except the destination of wafers is the receive cassette instead of the scrubber. Other than the wafer destination, the auto cycle steps are the same. Cassette ID, Slot ID, and Scrubber recipe ID are not used. However, they are saved so that they are available for a subsequent scrubber transfer cycle.
NOTE: The 6DS-SP "No. of Wafers" choice is not supported when using AGV.

===== [p263-264] 6DS-SP SOFTWARE VERSION 4.32 NEW FEATURES / INSTALLATION > Version 4.32 adds the following miscellaneous improvements: (12块) =====
--[p263]-- This prevents any situation where the arm could coincidentally be at "zero" position over the table center but considered safely at an "outer" position. If there is an attempt to move the arm to an "inner" or "outer" position with its value at zero, the arm will move, but will show an alarm as "not arriving".
Made correction to operation of start button when in screen idle or wet idle. The start button will no longer start the cycle when the idle is still occurring.
--[p264]-- Made improvement to operation when using the "misloaded wafers" alarm with the alarm action set to "halt". If the differential vacuum testing between the two carriers was fluctuating near the set point, it was possible to trigger the alarm but not immediately halt. This permitted the next step in the auto cycle sequence to occur which was to lower the spindles. Now, if the error occurs even briefly, the halt will occur without further sequence steps.
--[p264]-- Previously, this could be a problem if a forced slurry flush was occurring during idle or if the "Alt-L" feature was enabled. If neither the forced slurry flush nor the "Alt-L" feature is used, a normal (longer than a quick tap) pressing of the start button will cause an exit of the wet idle and a start of the cycle if the current menu is either the Auto Polish or Auto Polish Parameter menu.
--[p264]-- Previously, after both the load and unload stations had wafers, a second set of wafers would be loaded onto the load stations. The sequence will now load and unload wafers properly as if polishing had occurred.
Made correction for side-to-side throughput configuration so that it could operate with all polish times set to zero (for wafer handling testing without polishing). Previously, the cycle would go to wet idle after unloading wafers from spindles.
--[p263]-- Corrected problem where, on F-B throughput odd wafer polish, the "Odd Wafer Polish" status line display did not change until late in the cycle. It now changes at the same time the cycle actually makes the odd polish decision.
Added change to prevent setting conditioning arm "inner" and "outer" position flags if the corresponding recipe "inner" or "outer" value is zero.
--[p263]-- Version 4.32 adds the following miscellaneous improvements:
The GEM Process State reported a wet idle start only after the wet idle ended instead of when it started. This now works properly.
The automatic decision regarding which tables to use in an automatic cycle (based on nonzero times for a table) will now be made only when the machine is idle.
--[p263]-- If recipe changes are made during a cycle that would introduce a time for a table that had previously had all times zero, or vice versa, the change will be ignored until the current automatic cycle ends. This effectively prevents "number of tables used for processing" changes when the machine is running.
--[p264]-- Made change to ensure flag 108 "TBL2 has steps" and flag 505 "T2 long prestrt" are off in single table machines. Previously, even with no second table, second table polish time recipe values (which would not show but could be in the recipe) would turn on flag 108. Setting calibration variable 213 "Long T2 only prestart" to "1" would turn on flag 505.
--[p263]-- Corrected problem where the displayed wafer quantity would count down two wafers during an odd polish cycle instead of only one wafer. Wafer quantity will now count down only one wafer during an odd polish cycle.
Corrected problem where the wafer life counters would count up two wafers during an odd polish cycle instead of only one wafer. Wafer counting for pad, carrier and lifetime counters will now count up only one wafer during an odd polish cycle.
--[p264]-- Corrected nuisance "robot arms not at zero" alarm if using the wet idle feature of extending the robot arm over the scrubber sprayer. This alarm would briefly show when pressing the start button or remotely commanding a start. Once the arms returned to zero, the alarm stopped. This nuisance alarm will no longer occur.
Made correction to F-B throughput configuration operation when no polish times used (for wafer handling testing without polishing).
--[p263]-- Corrected problem in a two table configuration where both tables are used for polishing and the sequence to move the shuttle rear during primary polishing could not finish (such as due to a failure of the robot to move). After polishing, the spindles would remain on the table at minimum pressure indefinitely. Now, the spindle will raise and the automatic cycle will then stall until the shuttle move sequence problem is resolved.
--[p264]-- While there had never been a reported problem (these flags shouldn't effect single table sequences), it was decided it was best to make sure they were off if there is no second table.
Made a correction where, in some configurations, if there were no polish steps set (for wafer handling testing without polishing) the spindles would continue rotating after completing the rinse sequence after wafer unloading. The spindles will now stop rotating after the rinse sequence.

--[p129]-- MANUAL CONTROL MENU (screen page 1):
This menu/page allows manual manipulation of every system involved with wafer handling. If an illegal choice is made, a warning will show. If any choice is made, Stat: will change to Manual Mode.
If the entry area shows a dashed line, then a choice has not yet been made. If an entry area shows a choice, then that choice will be continuously asserted (with the exception of elevators).
--[p129]-- For example, if the bridge was commanded to move to the load position but is stopped because the polish door is opened, the bridge will continue to the load station when the door is closed.
The status of any item that has either servo position checks or physical switches is shown to the right of the selection area.
If the machine is idle, even "active" elevators can be moved. This can sometimes be useful for error recovery or to advance a send elevator past many empty slots.

===== [p371-371] 6DS-SP SOFTWARE VERSION 4.23.1 NEW FEATURES / INSTALLATION > Miscellaneous F-B Throughput Improvements: (2块) =====
--[p371]-- If using "demand wafer unload", if the "Use Throughput" choice in the Machine Setup menu is set to "disabled", wafers will be unloaded to the load stations instead of the unload stations.
--[p371]-- Miscellaneous F-B Throughput Improvements:
Version 4.23 adds some minor improvements for F-B throughput machines.
The polish door lock will now be released after F-B shuttle moves are complete.

===== [p260-260] 6DS-SP SOFTWARE VERSION 4.32 NEW FEATURES / INSTALLATION > Always Lower Both Spindles for Wafer Unloading Added: (2块) =====
--[p260]-- Always Lower Both Spindles for Wafer Unloading Added:
Version 4.32 adds the feature to "lower both spindles during wafer unloading". This is in addition to the "lower both spindles during wafer loading" choice previously added in version 4.31.
This feature now means "lower both spindles during either wafer loading or unloading".
--[p260]-- This choice is available to ensure that both load stations (and unload stations if using the high throughput option) experience equal mechanical forces whether the polishing cycle uses both carriers or is in an "odd polish" cycle.
Calibration Variable 214 "Lower both spindles (0-n, 1-y)" disables/enables this choice.
Note: Do not set this choice if only one carrier is loaded.
There is no automatic checking for carrier presence regarding this choice and spindles will be lowered even without carriers.

===== [p414-415] 6DS-SP VERSION 4.18 NEW FEATURES / INSTALLATION > Jog Feature for Calibration/Configuration Menu (for technicians): (3块) =====
--[p415]-- Jogging is immediate, so use caution. Avoid pressing the jog choices accidentally or with a higher than desired jog increment.
To help prevent accidental jogging, the JOG NEG and JOG POS choices are "guarded" (surrounded) by the Smallr Jog and Larger Jog choices. This makes it harder to accidentally press the jogging choices when merely wanting the nearby Page Down or Sel Menu choices.
Finally, you cannot jog with more resolution than can be displayed with the result.
Also, normally expected small resolution jogs may be ignored if the variable is very high in comparison (such as trying to jog 80000 by 0.01).
--[p414]-- Jog Feature for Calibration/Configuration Menu (for technicians):
A "jog" feature has been added to the Calibration/Configuration menu. Jogging permits a variable to be changed by some pre-defined increment without the need to tediously reenter the number. Jogging is permitted only at the maintenance password level.
The menu now has added function key choices Smallr Jog, JOG NEG, JOG POS, and Larger Jog.
--[p414]-- Also, the currently selected jog increment is highlighted at the bottom of the menu area to make it easy to see the current setting. Pay close attention to the jog increment setting. Hint: Set it to ".001" when otherwise not being used.
Use the Smallr Jog and Larger Jog choices to decrease or increase the jog increment. Use the JOG NEG and JOG POS choices to jog the currently cursored variable. The new jogged value is subject to the same illegal value check as if it had been entered manually.

===== [p205-205] IMPORTANT GENERAL INFORMATION > Provision for Extra Wafer Fetch Vacuum Time: (5块) =====
--[p205]-- If set to zero: The cycle will perform with the built-in 0.75 second delay after turning on end effector vacuum to sense a wafer in a cassette followed by a one time wafer presence check. This is how the 6DS-SP has previously and normally operated.
If set to non-zero: For example, if set to 1.25 seconds, after the 0.75 built-in delay is finished, the cycle will wait an additional 1.25 seconds before determining "no wafer".
--[p205]-- Provision for Extra Wafer Fetch Vacuum Time:
Version 4.36 adds the capability to set extra vacuum stabilization delay when the robot end effector is searching for wafers in a cassette. This can be used to protect wafer fetch sensing from short vacuum sags or to extend the time if vacuum is building slowly at the end effector.
The typical wafer fetch cycle turns on end effector vacuum and waits 0.75 seconds for vacuum stabilization.
--[p205]-- If at any time during that added 1.25 seconds the wafer is detected, the cycle is continued. Therefore, that entire additional 1.25 seconds may not be used.
CAUTION: Extra vacuum stabilization time may reduce overall throughput. But it may have no affect on throughput if using a High Throughput Option since all wafer unloading/loading may still be completed before polishing ends.
--[p205]-- Also, if many empty slots must be searched, the search time can be substantially extended because the entire extra time will be used for each search of an empty slot.
--[p205]-- Then it checks the end effector vacuum switch and determines whether or not a wafer is detected. If for any reason the switch is off, the decision is "no wafer".
You can now set an extra amount of time beyond the initial 0.75 seconds for the cycle to continue to test for vacuum before determining "no wafer".
Calibration variable 239 "Extra wfr fetch vac time(secs)" determines this extra time.

===== [p176-176] IMPORTANT GENERAL INFORMATION > Changes to Automatic Setting of Screen Colors (for technicians): (3块) =====
--[p176]-- During processing, this could lead to a nuisance alarm. Also, the software might also quit to DOS. Since previous software reset the screen colors with every attempt to select a menu, this could cause problems during normal operation when roaming among screens.
The setting the screen colors now occurs only when the program is started, or for the first menu selection when returning from the Flopro debugger. The software might still occasionally quit to DOS at either time.
--[p176]-- However, if this is seen when starting the software, the software can simply be restarted. If when returning from the debugger, it would occur during a troubleshooting session rather than normal processing.
This change assures there are no attempts to set screen colors during any normal operation of the software. If anything occurs to change the color palette (all colors become unusual), you must either restart the software, or enter and leave the Flopro debugger followed by a menu select.
--[p176]-- Changes to Automatic Setting of Screen Colors (for technicians):
Version 4.38 changes how screen colors are automatically set. With certain hardware (Part #306382 CompDyn SCSI monitor with part #240392 new model of IBM 7588 computer first used in the 6DS-SP at about the time of this release) the setting of screen colors was found to cause DOS timekeeping to pause briefly. This caused a small but false increase of rpm values displayed for the next rpm calculation scan.

===== [p323-323] 6DS-SP SOFTWARE VERSION 4.28 NEW FEATURES / INSTALLATION > STRASBAUGH, INC. (3块) =====
--[p323]-- STRASBAUGH, INC.
Version 4.28 permits the Host to select a recipe to be queued for the next batch in an Auto Cycle. If the recipe source in the Setup menu is "GEM Queue", the 6DS-SP will expect a recipe to be selected by the GEM host prior to each batch. If a new recipe is not selected (or the same recipe re-selected) the cycle will not continue. The queue holds only one recipe name and it must be for the next batch.
The possible wafer sources are:
Cassette AGV sender
--[p323]-- The possible recipe sources are:
"Oper or GEM" where the recipe selection must be made when the machine is idle.   
"GEM Queue" where the GEM host selects a recipe for queuing an auto cycle.   
"AGV Sender" where recipes are selected by the AGV sender data interface.
The previously separate Setup menu Wafer Source and Recipe Source choices have been combined to permit only valid combinations (and not permit the illegal combination of Cassette as a wafer source but AGV as a recipe source).
--[p323 [表]]-- The Setup menu now shows the following choices (depending on installed options):
Wafer Source/Recipe Source (In Auto Cycle) | Cass/Oper or GEM
Cass/GEM Queue
AGV/Oper or GEM
AGV/GEM Queue AGV/AGV Sender

===== [p307-307] IMPORTANT ! > Bridge Lube Oil Control: (1块) =====
--[p307]-- Bridge Lube Oil Control:
Version 4.29.1 adds control for the bridge lubrication. Output 109 “Lube oil OFF” is intended to control a new relay with normally closed contacts controlling the bridge lubrication pump. Output 109 will be turned on during any idle causing the normally closed relay contacts to open and turn off the oiling pump. This prevents needless oiling.
If a required new relay and its associated wiring are not installed, the control of output 109 will have no effect.

--[p151]-- ALARM MANAGEMENT MENU:
The Alarm Management Menu logs the most recent 32 alarms, the most recent 16 polish aborts, and permits alarm action configuration. (Examples shown on this page and the next two pages.)
The alarm log is intended to be a troubleshooting aid. (It is not a machine history log.) Alarms are logged with the date, time, and lifetime wafer count. This log should be reviewed analytically to accurately determine the cause of the alarms.

SPECIAL NOTE: If you upgrade from a previous version, the older "move down" variables 38, 39, 48, and 49 are no longer used. However, they will still remain in the Calibration/Configuration disk file CALVARS.DAT. If you load a version older than 4.32, that older version will use the older variables and not the new ones.
--[p258]-- Previous variable (obsolete) New left spindle variable New right spindle variable

--[p258]-- You can then 1) perform a calibration for the older variables or 2) enter the higher of each pair of variables 217-224 into corresponding older variables to ensure sufficient downforce for both spindles.
--[p258 [表]]-- Previously, the same value applied to both spindles and differences in the left and right return spring forces could result in noticeable differences in forces to load and unload stations. (This would not have effected operation during polishing where the left and right spindles have always been handled individually with independent "pressure minimum" values.)
The following table shows the previous four "move down" calibration variables and the eight new variables that replace them.
--[p258]-- This can change the behavior of the machine because each older variable is used for two spindles and the values won't reflect any subsequent calibration changes in the new variables.
Therefore, it is best to enter "0" for variables 38, 39, 48, and 49 during the installation of version 4.32. If you then load an older version, it will be obvious that you need to recalibrate variables 38, 39, 48, and 49 because the spindles will never lower.
--[p258]-- 49 &quot;Spindles down thruput value&quot; | 223 &quot;L spndle down thruput value&quot; | 224 &quot;R spndle down thruput value&quot;
NOTE: When first installing this software version, transfer the single value from each obsolete "move down" variable to the corresponding new variables. This ensures the machine will behave exactly as it did before upgrading software. If this is not done, spindles will not lower.
--[p258]-- Independent Left and Right Spindle "Move Down" Variables:
Version 4.32 has changes to provide independent left and right "move down" variables for each spindle. The "move down" variables determine the force used to move spindles down to various positions in the machine such as moving down onto load stations. These changes obsolete variables 38, 39, 48, and 49 that had applied to both spindles.

--[p174]-- Also, the Host is prohibited from changing these parameters. However, testing showed that the ZT8904 would sometimes lock up when the GEM application was terminated and then restarted. To solve this, the ZT8904 is now rebooted in order for the changes to take affect reliably.

Technical Description of GEM changes (for technicians) (continued):
The program’s sequence of events for changing one of these parameters:
1.
--[p175]-- In this scenario the batch file causes the PC5 to jump the program flow back to the initialization of SECS driver and restarts the GEM application. In the case of the ZT8904 the Gem PC will simply be rebooted.
6. The GEM application is restarted, and once the communication between the Gem PC and the Machine PC is established the prompt from Step 4 is cleared.
--[p174]-- The serial driver is a TSR (Terminate and Stay Resident) application, and once it is running the only way to reconfigure its parameters is to execute the CfgSdr (Configure SDR) application. In the original release of GWGEM for DOS there was a function call into the serial driver to update these parameters on the fly. With the Version 3.50 release of GWGEM this library function was removed.
--[p175]-- If the correct version is not found, the GEM application will request the Machine PC to uploaded the new version of GemPc.Bat, and the application ReBoot.Com. Once these files have been uploaded the Gem PC will reboot itself.
--[p174]-- Now, to update the SECS parameters on the fly, it is necessary to “spawn” a process (suspend application execution until another application is completely executed) within which to run the CfgSdr application. Since the original application is only suspended while the spawned application is run, there must be sufficient memory available for all applications to be loaded simultaneously.
--[p175]-- The GEM application inserts the new setting into the Gem140.Cfg file (this file contains the SECS parameters). Then, depending on the PC type being used, the GEM application will either exit with an exit code of “2” (in the case of the PC5), or the application will force a reboot of the Gem PC (in the case of the Ziatech).
5. The batch file that controls the program flow of the Gem PC, GemPc.Bat, interprets the exit code from the GEM application.
--[p175]-- This change required updating the GEM application and the controlling batch file that reside on the Gem PC, as well as the uploading of the reboot utility to the Gem PC. The updated GEM application will be uploaded to the Gem PC in the normal automatic manner when the 6DS-SP software is updated. Once running, the GEM application will determine if it has the correct batch file installed.
--[p175]-- The operator inputs the new setting.
2. The setting is tested against established limits. If outside the acceptable range the request is rejected.
3. The Communications State is tested to ensure that SECS is disabled. If not disabled the request is rejected.
4. If the above tests are successfully passed the request is passed on to the GEM application, and a message is displayed informing the operator that the software is “Re-configuring the Gem PC serial driver…”.
--[p174]-- On the newer SBS PC5 GEM PC, there is sufficient upper memory available to enable us to take advantage of memory management adjustments. However, the Ziatech ZT8904 Gem PC does not have any upper memory. While not all Ziatech Gem PC’s exhibited the memory problem at this time, it is only the matter of 1KB or so that determines insufficient memory on this PC model.
--[p174]-- There is insufficient memory available to run the CfgSdr.Exe utility while the XxxGem application is executing. The SBS PC5 computer can be configured to use upper memory to avoid this problem, but the Ziatech ZT8904 cannot.
Background – The SECS parameters control the operation of the low-level serial driver (SDR140.Exe) used to implement the SECS-I protocol.
--[p173]-- Change the parameter.
The change will be sent to the GEM PC which will exit the GEM application software (to make room in memory), run software to make the parameter change, and then restart the GEM application software (SBS PC5) or reboot the GEM PC (Ziatech ZT8904). This is all automatic.
The prompt “Re-configuring the Gem PC serial driver…” will show for a short period.   
When this prompt clears, SECS can be enabled again.
Technical Description of GEM changes (for technicians):
--[p174]-- The solution is to exit the GEM application, reconfigure the serial driver by running CfgSdr.Exe, and then restart the GEM application. As SECS parameters are critical to communications, and since they are normally only changed when the tool is being setup, it is reasonable to have the limitation that the parameters can only be changed when SECS is disabled. This way the cycling of the GEM application will not interfere with communication with a Host.

===== [p167-167] IMPORTANT GENERAL INFORMATION > New Prompts and More Information about the Reset Button: (5块) =====
--[p167]-- If the start button is pressed when a reset is required, the start button will be ignored.
If using spindle or table rotation on the Manual Control menu, entries will still be showing after a disabled polish section is reset – but rotation will not restart. Simply re-enter the desired value. This will cause a new velocity command to be sent to the servo controller (Non-CE equipped machines have always worked similarly after opening and closing a polish door.)
--[p167]-- On the Manual Control screen, if the polish section becomes disabled, any bridge or robot move choice will be automatically cancelled. This ensures the bridge or robot do not move upon pressing the reset button.
Note: This hardware-reset button is unrelated to the “Abort/Reset” function key choice on the menu that provides a software abort and reset.
(CE related changes continued on next page)
--[p167]-- New Prompts and More Information about the Reset Button:
Some new prompts will show in the prompt area of the screen when a reset is needed. These prompts will be in a bright blue color.
If halted and not requiring a reset, the following prompt shows:
Press START button to resume from halt.
If halted and a reset is required, the following prompt shows:
Press RESET, then START buttons to resume from halt.
--[p167]-- Opening and closing the doors and using the reset button should reliably cause the servo controllers to reset every time. However, if some sequence of events leaves the servo controller’s stuck in a “motor off” state (no servo action is seen when expected), use the F10 Abort/Reset choice. This should reset them to “on” if the polish section is not disabled. The Alt-T choice will show a special servo status screen where you can view the “Motor On” status.
--[p167]-- If the reset button does not cause a reset, re-open and re-close one of the polish section doors. The reset button should then work. (If a door is only partially opened, the action of the magnetic interlock switches may cause the safety relay to disable systems, but not be in a state to accept a reset.) Note: If the reset button does not work, it is not a software problem – it is an electrical problem.
If resetting is needed, use reset button before attempting to use the start button.

===== [p251-251] 6DS-SP SOFTWARE VERSION 4.33 NEW FEATURES / INSTALLATION > Version 4.33 adds the following miscellaneous improvements: (4块) =====
--[p251]-- Made correction for two table configurations using only the primary table for polish to correctly use the primary table "pressure minimums" (variables 32 and 42) after polishing before the spindles are raised from the table. Previously, the secondary table "pressure minimums (variables 37 and 47) had been used.
Made correction to the F-B automatic cycle when a new send cassette is installed while "odd polish" is occurring.
--[p251]-- This corrected a problem that could inhibit the 6DS-SP from automatically establishing communication with the Host, and entering the Communication State "Communicating".
--[p251]-- Previously, after loading the next two wafers to be polished on the load stations, the cycle would attempt to unload wafers from both spindles even though only the left was used for the "odd polish". The cycle will now correctly unload from only the left spindle after odd polish at all times.
In GEM, made a correction to the Equipment Constant initialization routine.
--[p251]-- Version 4.33 adds the following miscellaneous improvements:
Made change to operation of alarm action feature so that actions would not be set unless the machine is actually in an automatic cycle. Previously, an alarm during idle could produce a result such as displaying "finish cycle" even though the machine is idle.

===== [p363-364] 6DS-SP SOFTWARE VERSION 4.23.1 NEW FEATURES / INSTALLATION > ViPRR Menu Items: (3块) =====
--[p364]-- The ring force will ramp to the desired Ring Force polish step value based on the Force Ramp value. However, a minimum ring force of 0.5 psi of ring pressure will be applied to the table surface regardless of the setting or ramping of the ring force polish parameter. This helps prevent wafer slipouts.
--[p363]-- ViPRR Menu Items:
The Auto Polish and Auto Polish Parameters menus now show Ring Force (whether or not the machine is equipped for ViPRR).
Ring Force uses the same units as Polish Force (psi or lbs). These units are set in the Machine Parameters menu under Polish/Ring force units.
The Force Ramp value will apply to ring force as well as polish force.
ViPRR Operation In Auto Cycle:
When a polishing cycle is first started, a carrier presence check is made.
--[p364]-- The check turns on the spindle vacuums and checks the spindle vacuum switches. Carrier(s) must be present according to the Spindles Used choice in the Machine Setup menu.
When not polishing, the ring force regulators are set to approximately 2 psi to make sure the retaining rings are fairly extended. This helps ensure proper wafer loading and unloading. This also helps prevent wafer slipouts.
During polishing, the ring force is controlled along with the polish force.

--[p107]-- MACHINE PARAMETERS MENU (screen page 1):
This menu/page permits setting the most commonly changed parameters for machine operation. (The other two screen pages for this menu contain parameters that are seldom changed.) These parameters can affect process and are therefore saved as part of the recipe. (Other machine settings can be found in the Machine Parameters and Calibration/Configuration menus.)
The Spindle Force Mode can be set for either constant pressure or constant temperature.
--[p107]-- In the constant pressure mode, the polish force will be whatever is entered in the Polish Parameters Menu. In the constant temperature mode, force will be varied to attempt to maintain the pad temperature to the value entered in Pad Temperature. If the constant pressure mode is used, the Pad Temperature value is ignored.
The Left Force Scaling and Right Force Scaling values will cause the actual polish force to differ from the polish parameter force by the percent entered.
--[p107 [表]]-- The displayed polish force in the status area will not show this percentage difference. Only the actual force applied to the table will be different. This scaling intended to compensate for left/right polish differences that are process related. They should not be used to compensate for differences that are due to miscalibration of the machine.

===== [p87-136] USER INTERFACE REFERENCE > MENU ITEM DESCRIPTIONS: (89块) =====
--[p98]-- Ex-situ conditioning sequence occurs once when an automatic cycle and will not occur again so long as the machine remains in that automatic cycle. Sets the table speed during ex-situ conditioning. Positive values will cause counter-clockwise rotation.

===== [p406-406] 6DS-SP VERSION 4.18 NEW FEATURES / INSTALLATION > For technicians: (3块) =====
--[p406]-- For technicians:
The following calibration variables have been added to support the second conditioner:
121 "Cond2 park position"
This is the value in counts that will place the arm at the park position.
122 "Cond2 offset"
This is the value in counts that is set to cause the arm to be at 7 inches from the table center when commanded to be at 7 inches.
123 "Cond2 counts per inch"
This value is based on the hardware dimensions.
--[p406]-- It is actually one eleventh of the counts required to move the device from a point tangent to an 11" radius to a point on a line bisecting the table center. It must be set to 2192 for either the 2" or 4" conditioner.
127 "Cond2 coefficient"
An equation uses this value to adjust for the fact that the arm does not sweep a path that would intersect with the table center. It must be 0.02 for the 2" device and 0.04 for the 4" device.
--[p406]-- The calibration procedure is the same as that for the primary table conditioner. Make sure the table is in the polishing position (shuttle back). To summarize the procedure: Move the arm to an "inner" or "outer" position that has been set for 7 inches and adjust the offset so that the center of the device is exactly 7 inches from the table center.

===== [p356-356] NEW FEATURES / INSTALLATION > Correction to Odd Polish with HTO: (1块) =====
--[p356]-- Correction to Odd Polish with HTO:
Version 4.24 has a correction to the odd polishing cycle if using the high throughput option. Previously, the right hand wafer of the next to the last cycle could have incorrect polish force and the odd wafer an incorrect polish time. Both of these situations are now corrected.

===== [p245-245] 6DS-SP SOFTWARE VERSION 4.33 NEW FEATURES / INSTALLATION > Left and Right Force Scaling now Affects Ring Force: (1块) =====
--[p245]-- Left and Right Force Scaling now Affects Ring Force:
Version 4.33 makes a change so that force scaling from the Machine Parameters menu, page 1, modifies both polish and ring force together instead of polish force only.
It was determined that it is best to maintain the ratio of polish to ring force if using force scaling. Also, any effect on existing process was determined to be negligible. (This change is associated with the "odd polish force" feature described below.)

===== [p407-407] 6DS-SP VERSION 4.18 NEW FEATURES / INSTALLATION > Signal Descriptions: (3块) =====
--[p407]-- When the 11th step starts, it can then be known that secondary table polishing has started.
Two table machine with several timed steps on each table:
Two table machine with several timed steps on each table with an actual abort during primary table polishing:
Endpt Pol Start
Endpt Pol Abort
--[p407]-- Signal Descriptions:
"Endpt Pol Start" is turned on when polishing starts for the first table with any non-zero step times. It is turned off when polishing ends on the last table with any non-zero step times. It is also turned off with an abort.
"Endpt Pol Abort" is pulsed 2 seconds when polishing ends on the either table. It is also pulsed with an abort.
"Endpt Pol Step" is pulsed 1/2 second each time a new polish step starts for a table that has any non-zero step times.
--[p407]-- This output functions independently of the start and abort (end) outputs. However, if an actual abort occurs, polish step pulsing is also aborted. A table with any non-zero steps is considered to have 10 steps even if some have zero times. Zero time steps advance almost instantaneously so the output pulses may lag behind but will eventually "catch up" to the actual number of steps that occurred.
For two table polishing, the endpoint system should count all 10 primary table steps.

--[p452]-- 3) Make sure there is no force whatsoever on the condition force load cell.
4) Add any error seen in the "Cond (force)" value displayed in the status area to whatever is currently in variable 74. The "Cond" display should now read zero.
5) Re-enter the original dead weight value (recorded in step 2) into variable 71.
6) Return the condition force units in the Conditioning/Cleaning menu to "psi" if it had been changed to "lbs".
Additional reference information:

===== [p338-338] 6DS-SP SOFTWARE VERSION 4.26.1 NEW FEATURES / INSTALLATION > Overall hardware design: (2块) =====
--[p338]-- Overall hardware design:
The entire system consists of the 6DS-SP, an AGV interface, the AGV sender, and a scrubber. The AGV interface is between the 6DS-SP and the AGV sender. The sender gets wafers from the AGV provided cassette and delivers them to the 6DS-SP one at a time. After polishing, wafers can be sent to the scrubber. The 6DS-SP does not directly get wafers from the AGV provided cassettes.
--[p338]-- Wafers can also come from the send cassette inside the 6DS-SP and/or be delivered to the receive cassette inside the 6DS-SP. Also, if the scrubber fails, polished wafers will be automatically sent to the receive cassette.

===== [p346-346] 6DS-SP SOFTWARE VERSION 4.26.1 NEW FEATURES / INSTALLATION > Correction to Wet Idle Start for S-S HTP: (1块) =====
--[p346]-- Correction to Wet Idle Start for S-S HTP:
Version 4.26 corrects automatic wet idle starting in machines with the side-to-side high throughput option. The wet idle start should now wait until ex-situ conditioning is finished.
Previously, with long ex-situ conditioning, the automatic wet idle could start before conditioning finished. The conditioning would then not finish.

--[p73]-- NOTE:
This software is intended to support virtually all 6DS-SP options. Therefore, some options shown on menus may not apply to a specific machine.

--[p166]-- Front Panel Reset Button:
If the machine is CE equipped, a “reset” button is next to the “start” button.
When the polish door is opened, major systems in the polish section are disabled. These systems are the table/spindle/bridge/robot servo systems and the shuttle/spindle pneumatic systems. After closing the polish doors, these systems remain disabled until reset with the front panel reset button. While disabled, a reminder notice will show on the screen where the life data normally shows.
--[p166]-- If none of the above is occurring, then the life data shows (light blue background). This is the lowest priority use of the life data area and is typically what shows most of the time.

===== [p460-460] 6DS-SP VERSION 4.14 NEW FEATURES / INSTALLATION > NOTE: (1块) =====
--[p460]-- NOTE:
It is important that all water introduced into the lines be thoroughly flushed out. Otherwise, the weight of a column of water may bear on the backside of the next wafer or water may drain into the machine's exhaust system.

===== [p426-426] 6DS-SP VERSION 4.16.3 NEW FEATURES / INSTALLATION > "Spindles Down Hard Value" Now Used for Carrier Loading: (3块) =====
--[p426]-- If the "Spindles down soft value" had been increased to make sure the spindles successfully lowered during carrier loading, the value can be returned to a lower value.
For reference, the various "down" calibration variables are used as follows to move spindles down:
Variable 38 "Spindles down soft value" - onto a table before polishing. - onto single table machine clean stations. - from the Manual Control menu. - for carrier unloading. - for wet idle.
--[p426]-- "Spindles Down Hard Value" Now Used for Carrier Loading:
The value from Calibration Variable 39 "Spindles down hard value" is now used to move the spindles down during carrier loading. (Previously the value from Calibration Variable 38 "Spindles down soft value" was used.)
This change makes sure the spindles will completely lower without the weight of carriers.   
Also, the higher downforce aids loading carriers with the "drop protection" feature.
--[p426]-- Variable 39 "Spindles down hard value" - onto single table load stations. - for carrier loading.
Variable 48 "Spindles down extra soft value" - onto two table machine load stations
Variable 49 "Spindles down thruput value" - onto the throughput option unload station.

===== [p330-331] 6DS-SP SOFTWARE VERSION 4.27 NEW FEATURES / INSTALLATION > Zone Backpressure Support: (6块) =====
--[p330 [表]]-- Recipe choices permit all combinations of disabling backpressure, using standard backpressure (same backpressure to both zones), or using zone backpressure.
The Machine Parameters Menu backpressure recipe choices are now:
Recipe item | Two table choices | Single table choices
Backpressure (TBL# &amp; type) | Disable | Disable
TBL1&amp;2 std | TBL1 std
1std/2dis
2std/1dis
1&amp;2 zone | TBL1 zone
1zone/2dis
2zone/1dis
1zone/2std
2zone/1std
--[p330]-- Zone Backpressure Support:
Version 4.27 adds support for the zone backpressure option. This option supports carriers with two backpressure zones as well as single zone carriers. During polishing, one zone can have backpressure while the other zone is vented to atmosphere. Both zones are always used for vacuum, blowoff, and flushing. Output 110 "LT zone backprs" and output 111 "RT zone backprs" control the optional solenoid valves for venting zones to atmosphere.
--[p331]-- NOTE: Carrier configuration and backpressure choices must match.
For a two zone configured carrier, a zone backpressure choice must be used for at least one table. (Otherwise, the BP2 zone will be vented to atmosphere when not polishing resulting in improper wafer pickup, wafer blowoff, and flushing.)
For a single zone configured carrier, zone backpressure choices must not be used. (Otherwise, the BP2 line may fill up with water since it is plugged at the carrier.)
--[p330]-- Backpressure can be disabled ("dis"), standard ("std"), or zone. The first four choices shown have the same meaning as previous software versions although the text is changed. They should be used for single zone carriers. For example, "TBL1 only" now shows "1std/2dis" meaning table 1 uses standard backpressure and table 2 has backpressure disabled. The remaining five choices support zone backpressure combinations for two zone carriers.
--[p330 [表]]-- BP2 is always connected by a valve to either BP1 or atmosphere.
The BP2 backpressure system is controlled by the valve as follows:
Carrier configuration Polishing Vacuum Blowoff Idle
Two zones (must choose azone backpressure choice) | BP2 vented | BP2 to BP1 | BP2 to BP1 | BP2 to BP1
Single zone (must notchoose a zonebackpressure choice) | BP2 vented(isolates BP2) | BP2 vented(isolates BP2) | BP2 vented(isolates BP2) | BP2 vented(isolates BP2)
--[p330]-- For single table machines, only relevent single table choices show.
The zone backpressure system has two zones called "BP1" and BP2". One zone is in the center of the wafer mounting plate and the other around the outside. The machine can be plumbed with BP1 for the center (more pressure in the center) or BP1 for the outside (more pressure on the outside). BP1 is the E-P controlled backpressure system that also provides vacuum and blowoff.

===== [p189-189] IMPORTANT GENERAL INFORMATION > Alarm and Cycle Start Inhibit if "Stroke Limit" and "Slide & Lift" are Both Selected: (3块) =====
--[p189]-- NOTE: Alarm #49 will not actually show on the screen or the alarm log because the higher priority alarm #225 supercedes it. However, if an attempt is made to start a cycle, the cycle start is inhibited. Also, even though it won't show on the screen, this alarm will be reported to a GEM host.
--[p189]-- Alarm and Cycle Start Inhibit if "Stroke Limit" and "Slide & Lift" are Both Selected:
Version 4.37 adds new alarms for the case where both the "Slide & Lift" and "Table 1 Stroke Limit" features are both enabled. The slide & lift feature will move the bridge far beyond the table 1 stroke limit. Therefore, this combination of features is not permitted.
The calibration variables involved, and their settings to produce the alarms, are:
--[p189]-- 141 "Lift off(0-lift, 1-slide&lift)" = 1 and 236 "TBL1 stroke limit(0:6in,1:1in)" = 1
There are two new alarms (each has the same text):
Miscellaneous alarm #225 "STROKE LIMIT AND SLIDE&LIFT BOTH ENABLED" Cycle Start alarm #49 "STROKE LIMIT AND SLIDE&LIFT BOTH ENABLED"
Alarm #225 will show continuously (unless a higher priority alarm is showing) until th e settings of Calibration Variables 141 and/or 236 are changed.

===== [p172-172] IMPORTANT GENERAL INFORMATION > New Light Tower Control Configuration for Any Two Cassette Machine: (3块) =====
--[p172]-- Red Yellow | halted) Alarm Port empty | (never) Receive | Not alarm All ports filled
Cassette Ready to Be removed Because all Wafers set in “No. of Wafers&quot; are polished and cycle went idle (Has priority over “port empty”) | And being used
--[p172]-- New Light Tower Control Configuration for Any Two Cassette Machine:
Version 4.38 adds a new light tower configuration for a three light tower. This light tower configuration supports only 6DS-SP configurations with a single send cassette and a single receive cassette (S-S HTP, Nova + Scrubber, AGV).
The yellow light will blink when the receive cassette is ready to be removed based on the operator using the “No.

When the receive cassette arm is lifted to remove the cassette, the “ready to be removed” status will be cleared and the yellow light will stop blinking.

===== [p171-171] IMPORTANT GENERAL INFORMATION > Exhaust Fail Alarm (CE related): (2块) =====
--[p171]-- Exhaust Fail Alarm (CE related):
Version 4.38 adds alarm #44 “EXHAUST FAIL”. This reflects the status of input 72 “Exhaust fail”.
This input, if used, comes from either an exhaust gas flow monitor on the machine or from some other monitoring device in the facility.
All of the alarm actions are available for assignment in the Alarm Configuration area of the Alarm Management menu. Other than alarm actions, this alarm does not effect any other machine behavior.
--[p171]-- While this was added as a CE requirement, it can be used for any application whether or not the machine is CE equipped. There is no hardware change because it uses an existing input for any machine that has digital I/O mounting rack 4MR installed. This mounting rack includes Input 72.

===== [p332-332] 6DS-SP SOFTWARE VERSION 4.27 NEW FEATURES / INSTALLATION > AGV Automatic Start and New Transfer Request Wait Variable: (3块) =====
--[p332]-- However, if either the Auto Polish or Polish Parameter menu is selected, all conditions exist and the 6DS-SP will start. While it will appear as if menu selection alone caused the start, it was actually the existance of three conditions.
Also, version 4.27 adds Calibration variable 101 "AGV max xfer req wait (secs)" instead of the original fixed value set at 120 seconds in 4.26 and 240 seconds in 4.26.1.
--[p332]-- Note that these conditions do not have to occur in any particular order. They must only exist simultaneously. For example:
If the wafer source is set to "AGV Intrfc" and the Auto Polish menu is showing, the 6DS-SP will start when the AGV sender asserts a transfer request.
If the wafer source is set to "AGV Intrfc" and the AGV sender is already asserting a transfer request but neither the Auto Polish nor Polish Parameter menu is showing, the 6DS-SP won't start.
--[p332]-- AGV Automatic Start and New Transfer Request Wait Variable:
Version 4.27 adds automatic starting for the AGV equipped machine configuration.
The 6DS-SP will automatically start when all of the following occur:
\- The Machine Setup menu Wafer Source choice is set to "AGV Intrfc"
Either the Auto Polish or Polish Parameters menu is showing (the same menus required to start with the "start" pushbutton)
\- The AGV sender asserts a transfer request

===== [p321-321] 6DS-SP SOFTWARE VERSION 4.28 NEW FEATURES / INSTALLATION > Optional Wet Idle Robot to Scrubber Move: (2块) =====
--[p321]-- Optional Wet Idle Robot to Scrubber Move:
Version 4.28 permits moving the robot to a scrubber station and extending the arm into the station during wet idle. This places the end effector over a specially plumbed spray that is teed into the left load rinse line (or any other suitable DI water source). When the load rinse turns on in wet idle, some water will spray on the end effector. This spray can help prevent drying of any residual slurry on the end effector.
--[p321]-- This move will not be made if a wafer is on the end effector. Instead, the robot will simply move to the usual position nearest the elevator doors and the arm will not extend.
Set Calibration Variable 55 "Robt to scrb@wet idle(0-n,1-y)" to "1" to enable this feature and to "0" to disable.

===== [p412-412] 6DS-SP VERSION 4.18 NEW FEATURES / INSTALLATION > Post Loading Wafer Presence Test: (1块) =====
--[p412]-- Post Loading Wafer Presence Test:
If 15 seconds has passed after wafers are loaded onto the spindles and the wafers have not been detected, the following will now occur:
The cycle will halt.
An alarm message will show.
Any slurry turned on with the "Slurry Prestart" feature will be turned off.
If the wafers are detected at any time within the 15 seconds, the automatic cycle will continue normally.
(Previously, if wafers were not detected, the cycle would stall with no alarm message and prestart slurry sould continue to flow.)

===== [p219-219] IMPORTANT GENERAL INFORMATION > Support Lot Recipe Integrity in Non-HTP Configurations: (6块) =====
--[p219]-- For subsequent lots during the same automatic cycle, if a recipe is not received for a new lot the machine will go idle at the end of the previous lot with no alarm.
--[p219]-- The machine will not process a lot if it has not received a recipe name from the Host for that lot (even if recipe will be the same as the previous lot). When starting the machine to process the first lot, if a corresponding recipe has not been received from the Host, the alarm 82 "PP SELECTION NOT QUEUED" will show, the cycle will not start, and the machine will go to idle.
--[p219]-- Support Lot Recipe Integrity in Non-HTP Configurations:
Version 4.35 adds support of lot recipe integrity to non-HTP configurations (originally added in version 4.33 for HTP configurations only).
This feature applies only if using GEM. This feature permits processing each lot with a different recipe. Lot/recipe integrity is maintained even if lots have an odd number of wafers.
--[p219]-- For subsequent lots, once the last wafers of the previous lot are unloaded from the carriers AND the first wafers of the next lot are loaded onto the carriers AND any exsitu conditioning from the previous lot is complete, the queued recipe associated with the next lot is loaded and the cycle continues.
Note: Remember that ex-situ conditioning is part of the recipe and therefore is part of the processing time for a lot and its associated recipe.
--[p219]-- At the start of the auto cycle, the queued recipe is loaded to ensure that any possible pre polish recipe related actions occur.
\- The first lot starts processing.
\- Another lot can be placed in the machine while the previous lot is processing.
\- The Host then queues a recipe name for that next lot.
\- That first lot finishes processing and can be removed.
\- New lots with new Host queued recipes can be put in the machine indefinitely.
--[p219]-- If a lot has an odd number, an "odd wafer polish" cycle will finish that lot before starting the next one with a different recipe. Also a lot is defined as a single cassette for this feature.
To use this feature:
Calibration variable 41 "Lot integrity (0-disbl, 1-enbl)" must be set to "1".
Machine Setup menu "Wafer Source/Recipe Source" must be set to "Cass/GEM queue"
General sequence of events:
\- Place lot (cassette) in machine.
\- Host queues a recipe name to be used for that lot.

===== [p270-270] 6DS-SP SOFTWARE VERSION 4.31 NEW FEATURES / INSTALLATION > Carrier X Support: (4块) =====
--[p270]-- If the forces have the wrong relationship (too much membrane force versus too little spindle force) the carrier can raise causing wafer slipout. The proper force relationships must exist not only during polishing, but also during the start and end of polishing. When creating recipes or setting control gains, these forces should be observed in the status area to ensure reliable operation.
NOTE: For Carrier X, wafer diameter must be entered regardless of whether forces are shown in psi or lbs.
--[p270]-- Carrier X Support:
Version 4.31 adds support for "Carrier X". This carrier has a membrane that applies pressure to the wafer and a retaining ring that contacts the pad under pressure. The desired wafer and retaining ring forces are settable in the recipe polish parameters. Backpressure, zone backpressure, and spindle flushing are not used with Carrier X and do not show on any menus or the status display.
--[p270]-- The software always uses wafer diameter for Carrier X unit conversions.
NOTE: Carrier X uses latching mechanisms for carrier drop protection but the carrier vacuum is also still used to hold the carrier to the spindle.
--[p270]-- The theory of operation on the next page describes how the two controlled forces (membrane force and spindle down force) produce the two desired forces against the polishing pad (wafer force and retaining ring force).
NOTE: It is important to always have sufficient spindle force compared to membrane force. Spindle force is trying to push the carrier down to the table and membrane force has the opposite effect of trying to raise the carrier up from the table.

===== [p310-310] IMPORTANT ! > AGV Changes: (1块) =====
--[p310]-- AGV Changes:
Version 4.29.1 adds two new AGV tests and related alarms.
It also changes how the AGV Transfer Request Timeout is handled.
Alarm 229 “AGV DATA TRANSFER ERROR (abort clears)” means illegal data was received from the AGV sender.
Alarm 230 “AGV DATA TRANSFER TIMEOUT (abort clears)” means that ten seconds has elapsed and expected data from the AGV sender was not received.
Also, the AGV Transfer Request Timeout is now disabled after an AGV Lot End signal is received.
The timeout is again enabled when the next AGV wafer is received. This means alarms will no longer occur when the 6DS-SP is merely idle between lots.

===== [p423-423] 6DS-SP VERSION 4.16.3 NEW FEATURES / INSTALLATION > Choice of Spindle and Table Rotation Direction: (5块) =====
--[p423 [表]]-- Consider the following recipe steps for a machine with a 7.5:1 primary table ratio (only time, forces and speeds are shown):
Step 1 | Step 2 | Step 3
Left polish time | 180.0 | 2.0 | 180.0 | secs
Right polish time | 180.0 | 2.0 | 180.0 | secs
Polish force | 7.0 | 0.0 | 7.0 | psi
Left BkPrs | 1.0 | 0.0 | 1.0 | psig
Right BkPrs | 1.0 | 0.0 | 1.0 | psig
Table speed | 25.0ccw | 0.0ccw | -25.0 CW | rpm
Spindle speed | 25.0ccw | 0.0ccw | -25.0 CW | rpm
--[p423]-- Choice of Spindle and Table Rotation Direction:
The directions of spindle and table rotations can be chosen in the Polish Parameters menu. Also, table direction for conditioning can be chosen in the Conditioning/Cleaning Parameters menu and table direction for slurry prestart can be chosen in the Machine Parameters menu.
Direction is chosen by entering a positive value for counter-clockwise rotation and a negative value for clockwise rotation.
--[p423]-- In the example, the speed reduces to zero as the forces diminish. Then the force builds again as the spindles and table start turning in the opposite direction.
NOTE: If a spindle or table axis is still turning in one direction when commanded to go the other it will not immediately change direction. Instead, the axis will gradually decelerate to zero before changing direction and reaccelerating in the new direction.
--[p423]-- Clockwise and counter-clockwise are defined as viewed looking down on the machine.
The notation "cw" or "ccw" will show for parameters that permit choosing rotation direction. If the value is positive or zero "ccw" will show and if the value is negative "cw" will show. (Showing "cw" or "ccw" makes the direction choice easier to see compared to displaying only the minus sign.)
--[p423]-- If rotation direction is changed while maintaining full polish force, friction may dramatically increase when rotation slows resulting in broken wafers. It is best to reduce polish force and back pressure with an "in between" step before changing direction.
Approximate deceleration time for spindles and tables are as follows:
Spindles .05 sec/rpm Primary table (7.5:1 ratio) .04 sec/rpm Primary table (10:1 ratio) .05 sec/rpm Primary table (15:1 ratio) .08 sec/rpm Second table .04 sec/rpm

===== [p341-343] 6DS-SP SOFTWARE VERSION 4.26.1 NEW FEATURES / INSTALLATION > Description of AGV > Polish> Scrubber Mode: (12块) =====
--[p342]-- Otherwise, the 6DS-SP will not respond with "ready" until the existing wafers are polished and returned to the load stations. This provides maximum protection for the wafer by leaving it in the AGV unit until it is actually needed.

--[p342]-- 5) 6DS-SP automatically starts the "auto cycle" mode (if not already in an auto cycle).
6) If a 6DS-SP "start" alarm occurs, the 6DS-SP quits the cycle and returns to idle. As long as the alarm condition exists, steps 5 and 6 will be performed indefinitely until the 6DS-SP is aborted.
7) 6DS-SP attempts to receive wafer from AGV interface. If received, a "wafer present" flag is set. If the "wafer set" signal is not seen in 30 seconds, a 6DS-SP alarm shows.
--[p341]-- NOTE: Due to the requirement that the 6DS-SP automatically start when receiving a "transfer request", if any cycle start alarm condition occurs, the two equipments could be in a repetative "start-alarm-fail-start..." loop. (The 6DS-SP enters the "Auto" cycle before it checks for alarm conditions. When alarm conditions are found, the 6DS-SP quits the cycle.)
The following is a description of operator steps for the AGV > Polish > Scrubber auto cycle:
--[p342]-- Note: The 6DS-SP will wait 240 seconds for a transfer request. If there is no transfer request, the 6DS-SP will wait indefinitlely and show an alarm. If the transfer request occurs, the alarm will clear and the transfer cycle will continue.
8) If using AGV supplied recipes and the wafer is not the second wafer of a pair, the 6DS-SP attempts to load recipe. If the recipe is found - the cycle continues. If not found - an alarm shows that can only be aborted.
--[p342]-- 1) Operator makes sure the 6DS-SP is idle, in screen idle, in wet idle, or already started in an automatic cycle.
2) If AGV is the recipe source (Machine Setup menu), operator makes sure that the "Auto Cycle Operation" and "Active Spindles" choices currently showing match what is expected in AGV recipes.
3) Operator starts AGV and presses the remote 6DS-SP start button (or the start button on the 6DS-SP).
4) AGV turns on transfer request (6DS-SP will ignore if busy in maintenance, etc.)
--[p341]-- The scrubber recipe ID (1-99) will be whatever was in the 6DS-SP recipe used when the wafer was polished.
NOTE: The 6DS-SP "No. of Wafers" choice is not supported when using AGV. The 6DS-SP will continue to expect wafers from the AGV sender until a lot finishes processing and Transfer Requests are no longer received.
--[p341]-- After the AGV transfers a wafer to the 6DS-SP's AGV station, the 6DS-SP turns on a "wafer present" flag. When the 6DS-SP robot removes the wafer, the flag is cleared. An abort also clears the flag.
If the Machine Parameters menu "Recipe Source" is set to "AGV intrfc", the 6DS-SP attempts to load the AGV requested recipe. If single spindle polishing, the 6DS-SP will load a recipe for each wafer.
--[p342]-- If receiving the second wafer of a pair for dual polishing, the recipe ID is ignored and the first wafer's recipe is used for both.
9) 6DS-SP moves wafer to load station.
When removed from the AGV station, the "wafer present" flag is cleared. Another wafer can be immediately received from the AGV interface if it is the second of a pair of wafers for dual spindle polishing.
--[p343]-- 11) After polished wafers are unloaded into the load stations, the 6DS-SP will now respond to an AGV transfer request with "ready". AGV wafer transfer occurs simultaneously with sending polished wafers to the scrubber. This provides maximum throughput.
12) The polished wafers are sent to the scrubber.
13) If a wafer was received from the AGV while wafers were sent to the scrubber, the sequence repeats at step 6 with a wafer already on the 6DS-SP AGV station.
Otherwise, the sequence repeats at step 5 waiting for a wafer from the AGV interface.
--[p341]-- If these parameters are changed after the 6DS-SP is in an auto cycle, operation may not be correct. These are parameters are:
Auto Cycle Operation (Machine Parameters menu page 1)
Active Spindles (Machine Parameters menu page 1)
Once started, the 6DS-SP will expect wafers from the AGV indefinitely. However, if the last wafer from a lot has been processed and no further Transfer Request is received, the 6DS-SP will automatically go into a wet idle.
--[p341]-- If dual spindle polishing, the 6DS-SP will load the recipe for the first wafer and ignore the recipe for the second wafer. If the recipe is found, it is loaded and its name ("0" through "255") should immediately show on the 6DS-SP "Recipe" area. If not found, an alarm shows.
When the 6DS-SP delivers a wafer to the scrubber, its cassette ID, slot ID, and scrubber recipe ID are also transferred. The cassette and slot ID's will be what was originally received with the wafer from the AGV interface.
--[p341]-- Description of AGV > Polish> Scrubber Mode:
This is the most complicated automatic mode. The 6DS-SP, scrubber, and AGV must all be turned on. The 6DS-SP can be idle, in screen idle, in wet idle, or in an automatic cycle already (started with the "start" button or GEM). The 6DS-SP and scrubber must both be "inline" and not having an alarm.
If recipes from the AGV will be used, the recipe already showing on the 6DS-SP must have certain parameters match the expected AGV recipes.

--[p215]-- Importance of vacuum switch adjustments:
Steady chucking vacuum is continually monitored, even if using carrier latches, for all configurations except the two passage Viprr. Therefore, vacuum switches controlling inputs 5 and 6 must be properly adjusted.
If vacuum switches are misadjusted you may see errors such as "LEFT [RIGHT] VACUUM SWITCH OFF" or "LEFT [RIGHT] SPINDLE VACUUM NOT FOUND".
Also, the bridge amplifier is disabled if a spindle's chucking vacuum is on but its vacuum switch is off.

===== [p372-372] 6DS-SP SOFTWARE VERSION 4.23.1 NEW FEATURES / INSTALLATION > "Cassette ready to be removed" correction: (2块) =====
--[p372]-- Also, light tower configurations "2" and "3" were previously described as having the "Cassette ready to be removed" operation but actually provide a "Receive port empty or receive cassette ready to be removed" operation. The document "6DS-SP Calibration/Configuration Reference" has been changed to more accurately describe this operation.
--[p372]-- "Cassette ready to be removed" correction:
If a light tower is to indicate "Cassette ready to be removed", some machine/light tower configurations would not turn on the light properly. Instead, the light would be on any time the cassette arm was up. These configurations will now turn on the light when the cassette is ready to be removed and the light will turn off when the arm is raised. (This function should not turn on the light merely because the port is empty.)

===== [p304-304] IMPORTANT ! > Alarm Action Behavior: (2块) =====
--[p304]-- If an alarm action aborts polishing, the step number and remaining step time will automatically be placed in the abort log just as if the operator had aborted polishing.
--[p304]-- Alarm Action Behavior:
Action is continually asserted if an alarm exists with a configured action. Therefore, if the operator clears a halt or finish cycle and the alarm is still occurring, the action would immediately be re-asserted by the alarm. Remember, an alarm may not display if a higher priority alarm is showing although its action will still be asserted. If multiple action alarms exist, the alarm with the most severe action will be displayed. (Note: Multiple alarms are rare.)

===== [p173-173] IMPORTANT GENERAL INFORMATION > GEM Changes to Permit User Changes of SECS Parameter Constants: (1块) =====
--[p173]-- GEM Changes to Permit User Changes of SECS Parameter Constants:
Version 4.38 changes how the user sets SECS parameter equipment constants (Device ID, Baud Rate, Timers, and Retry Limit). These are parameters that are typically set only once during machine setup. Also, the Host is prohibited from changing these parameters.
These changes were required due to memory constraints in the Ziatech ZT8904 GEM computers. However, the same changes also apply to the newer SBS PC5 GEM computers.

===== [p206-206] IMPORTANT GENERAL INFORMATION > File Checking at Startup: (3块) =====
--[p206]-- Now, the utility program Chkfiles.exe is automatically run before running the main software. If Chkfiles.exe finds file trouble, a screen message notifies the operator who must then press any key. Then Chkfiles.exe creates a new file(s) so that the 6DS-SP can start successfully.
Newly created Errors.dat or Aborts.dat files won't have any data in them, but the data from the old file is known to be lost anyway.
--[p206]-- File Checking at Startup:
Version 4.36 adds a means to check the quality of certain files when the machine is started. These are the files for logging alarms (Errors.dat), logging aborts (Aborts.dat), and storing the currently used recipe name (Rec\_name.dat) as shown on the status line.
The 6DS-SP software cannot run if any of these files are missing or corrupted. While rare, this had required finding and installing a "healthy" file to solve the problem.
--[p206]-- A newly created Rec\_name.dat file will have the name "None" which will show on the status line. Simply select any recipe so that an actual recipe name will show with its data.

===== [p260-260] 6DS-SP SOFTWARE VERSION 4.32 NEW FEATURES / INSTALLATION > Force Spindle Flush Wafer Blowoff Choice: (2块) =====
--[p260]-- Force Spindle Flush Wafer Blowoff Choice:
Version 4.32 adds a choice to force using the spindle flush for wafer blowoff in configurations that would normally use standard wafer blowoff.
Calibration Variable 225 "Force flsh wfr blwoff(0-n,1-y)" disables/enables this choice.
Note, enabling will override the automatic decision to use the standard blowoff. Disabling will not override an automatic decision to use the spindle flush wafer blowoff.
--[p260]-- Disabling only means the forced override won't occur and won't have any effect on configurations with Hydro Lift load stations and/or when using throughput unload stations. These configurations automatically use spindle flush wafer blowoff regardless.

===== [p431-432] 6DS-SP VERSION 4.16.3 NEW FEATURES / INSTALLATION > Endpoint Carrier Presence Detection for Cable Protection: (8块) =====
--[p432]-- The second wafer is now held in the scrubber flipper and rinsed. Also, two different handling sequences are possible based on the setting of a new "busy" timeout.
Calibration Variable 156 “Scrubber type (0-DNS,1-OnTrak)” must be set to “1” if an OnTrak scrubber is attached.
Calibration Variable 157 “OnTrak busy timeout (secs)” is applicable only to the OnTrak scrubber and is used only when polishing with both spindles as follows:
--[p432]-- New Post Polish Wafer Cleaning Choices for Two Table Machines:
New post polish wafer cleaning choices have been added to the Conditioning/Cleaning menu. These choices permit wafer cleaning after polishing on either table or both. The choices will now show as:
--[p431]-- If an endpoint carrier’s cable is plugged into the receptacle on the spindle but the carrier chuck vacuum is not sensed, the bridge amplifier will be disabled preventing bridge moves. Also, the auto cycle will be prevented from starting. Finally, Manual menu bridge moves will be prevented.
This change supersedes the previous wafer handling where the second of two polished wafers remained held on the robot for an extended time while the scrubber processes the first wafer.
--[p431]-- (NOTE: If set to “1” and endpoint carriers are not installed, false error detection may occur.)
If variable 19 is set to “1” inputs 35 “EPt Lt Lsr Pres” and 36 “EPt Rt Lsr Pres” will be monitored at all times for the purpose of this bridge move protection. These inputs turn on when their respective carrier cables are plugged in.
--[p432]-- When the first of the two polished wafers is still in the scrubber's first cleaning station, the scrubber cannot accept the second wafer. The second wafer will be placed in the scrubber flipper, rinsing starts, and the "OnTrak busy timeout" starts.
If the scrubber becomes "ready" (first wafer clears the scrubber's first cleaning station) before the "busy" timeout, the second wafer is transferred to the scrubber. Then the auto cycle continues to handle the next unpolished wafers.
--[p431]-- Endpoint Carrier Presence Detection for Cable Protection:
Calibration Variable 19 “Endpt carr present(0-no, 1-yes)” determines if endpoint carrier detection for cable protection will occur. This protection prevents bridge moves in the case where an endpoint carrier is unloaded but its cable is still connected. A bridge move at that time could rip the cable apart.
Set variable 19 to “1” if endpoint carriers are installed.
Set variable 19 to “0” if endpoint carriers are not installed.
--[p432]-- 1) Ensuring both wafers are transferred before the auto cycle continues: A "busy" timeout that is comfortably longer than the "ready" waiting time will make sure both polished wafers are transferred before the next wafers are handled.
2) Maximizing throughput: A "busy" timeout that is shorter than the "ready" waiting time will force the 6DS-SP to continue autocycling at the end of the "busy" time. Therefore, this time should be set to "0" for the fastest throughput.
--[p432]-- If the "busy" timeout occurs before the scrubber becomes "ready", the auto cycle starts handling the next unpolished wafers with the second polished wafer stored in the flipper. When the scrubber subsequently becomes ready (first wafer clears the first cleaning station) the second wafer is transferred to the scrubber.

--[p380]-- Support for Slurry Flow Sensing Option:
Version 4.22 adds support for a slurry flow sensing option. This option has flow sensors installed between the slurry pumps and the delivery point. Setpoint modules monitor the sensors and control 6DS-SP inputs 75 (for slurry 1), 76 (for slurry 2), and 77 (for slurry 3). An input represents whether or not slurry flow is above the value calibrated in the corresponding setpoint module.
--[p380]-- Pressing the start button will let the Auto Cycle continue and clear the alarm. An abort will also clear the alarm.

===== [p96-96] USER INTERFACE REFERENCE > SWEEP PARAMETERS MENU (continued): (3块) =====
--[p96]-- Simply enter the desired time or force anwhere in the column and make sure the cursor is resting on that value. Press the function key to cause all 20 segment entries to equal the cursored entry.
--[p96]-- However, changes to arm speeds have accelerations and decelerations so instant speed changes are not possible. Also, due to the scan rate of the software, if the sweep segment time is too short, the arm may traverse the segment before the software recognizes it. A suggested minimum time is 0.5 seconds.
The Colmn = Cursor function key can be used to avoid tedious repetitive number entry if all times or all forces will be the same.
--[p96]-- SWEEP PARAMETERS MENU (continued):
The sweep range is from the "outer" to the "inner" position. This range has 20 segments. Segment 1 is at the outer position and segment 20 is at the inner position. Each segment has its own time and force. (The second conditioner has times only and uses a fixed pressure regulator.)
By varying the times and/or forces, almost any linear or non-linear sweep behavior can be generated.

===== [p461-461] 6DS-SP VERSION 4.14 NEW FEATURES / INSTALLATION > Two Table Machine Wafer Cleaning and Carrier Pad Cleaning: (3块) =====
--[p461]-- If Carrier Cleaning is enabled, after the robot removes a polished wafer its load station, that station's fountain rinse will turn on and the carrier will rotate. This will continue for the period entered in Carrier Cleaning Time. Carrier cleaning will occur only if the cycle is "Auto". It will not occur if the cycle is "Manual" or "Condition". Also, if spindle flushing is enabled, it will start at the same time as carrier cleaning so that both functions run concurrently to minimize cycle time.
Loading of the next wafer to be polished is inhibited until both spindle flushing and carrier cleaning are finished.
--[p461]-- Post Polish Wafer Cleaning Enable/Disable Wafer Cleaning Time 0 secs
Carrier Cleaning (Auto only) Enable/Disable Carrier Cleaning Time 0 secs
If Post Polish Wafer Cleaning is enabled, the bridge will move polished wafers to the load stations, the fountain rinses will turn on and the carriers will rotate. This will continue for the period entered in Wafer Cleaning Time. When finished, the wafers will be unloaded and the cycle will continue with the original rinsing of the unloaded wafers.
--[p461]-- Two Table Machine Wafer Cleaning and Carrier Pad Cleaning:
This feature requires fountain rinses at the load stations that have been modified to have a spray pattern that is essentially straight up. Wafer or carrier pad cleaning is accomplished by using these fountain rinses with the spindles up over the load stations.

===== [p425-425] 6DS-SP VERSION 4.16.3 NEW FEATURES / INSTALLATION > Throughput Improvement When Using Pre-conditioning: (2块) =====
--[p425]-- NOTE: Conditioning for the next wafers to be polished starts when the previous polished wafers are being unloaded. If a "finish cycle" is requested, a conditioning cycle will still occur when the wafers are unloaded. When a new auto cycle is started, a preconditioning cycle will again occur before polishing wafers. Therefore, it is possible to have two conditioning cycles occur prior to polishing wafers.
--[p425]-- Throughput Improvement When Using Pre-conditioning:
If pre-conditioning is used, a conditioning cycle will start when the "start" button is pressed and the robot is getting wafers from the send cassette(s).
So long as the machine is permitted to automatically cycle, subsequent conditioning cycles will start shortly after polishing at the same point that post conditioning normally occurs. This makes sure conditioning always starts as early in the cycle as possible.

===== [p362-363] 6DS-SP SOFTWARE VERSION 4.23.1 NEW FEATURES / INSTALLATION > ViPRR Hardware Configuration: (3块) =====

This is the force applied to the table by the weight of the retaining ring and bladder.
--[p362]-- ViPRR Hardware Configuration:
A 6DS-SP equipped for ViPRR carriers has valves that route either vacuum or retaining ring pressure to one of the pneumatic channels in the spindles. The vacuum is used during carrier loading and unloading. The ring pressure is open loop controlled by 0-20 psi regulators. (The actual ring pressure on the table is determined by the ring area and an empirical coefficient.) Ring pressure is also used as blowoff for carrier loading and unloading.

===== [p438-438] 6DS-SP VERSION 4.16.3 NEW FEATURES / INSTALLATION > Loading from a send cassette: (2块) =====
--[p438]-- Loading from a send cassette:
1) In the 6DS-SP’s Machine Parameters menu set for “Left Spindle Only”.
2) In the 6DDS-SP’s Polish Parameters menu set all polish times to “0”.
3) In the 6DS-SP’s Auto Polish menu set to polish one wafer.
4) Place the wafer in the top slot of a cassette and place the cassette in the send station.
5) Place a receive cassette in the 6DS-SP.
6) Start the 6DS-SP when ready.
--[p438]-- The wafer will be loaded from the send cassette, loaded onto the spindle, immediately unloaded, placed in the Nova station, “learned”, and then removed from the Nova station and placed in the receive cassette.

===== [p245-245] 6DS-SP SOFTWARE VERSION 4.33 NEW FEATURES / INSTALLATION > Left and Right Force Scaling Effects Now Show on Status Display of Polish Force: (3块) =====

Item Previous values New values

Version 4.33 makes a change to how polish force is displayed when the left and right force scaling is not set to 100%. There is no change to actual force due to scaling - only how it is displayed. This is the force scaling set in Machine Parameters menu page 1. (This change is associated with the "odd polish force" feature described below.)
