===== [p312-313] SLURRY PH TRANSMITTERCALIBRATION > B. CHECK AND WET CALIBRATE THE TRANSMITTER (4块) =====
--[p313 [表]]-- • Using a small screwdriver, rotate the adjusting screw labeled R21 as needed until the transmitter’s display meets the goal.
9. Rinse the pH electrode in clean water and dry with a clean cloth.
10. Submerse the pH electrode into the pH 10 value buffer solution, gently stirring the solution for a few seconds, allowing the transmitter’s LCD display to stabilize.
11. While monitoring the transmitter’s LCD display, adjust the slope potentiometer:
--[p313]-- GOAL #2: | The display must read within +/- 0.1 pH of 10 while the transmitter&#x27;s electrode is immersed in a pH 10 buffer solution.
• Using a small screwdriver, rotate the adjusting screw labeled R25 as needed until the transmitter’s display meets the goal.
12. Repeat Steps 6. through 11. to check the correction. If needed, repeat the adjustments until both goals are met.
13. When both goals have been met, reinstall the transmitter.
--[p312]-- B. CHECK AND WET CALIBRATE THE TRANSMITTER
1. Prepare the pH buffer solutions by filling a small beaker with one inch of each solution.
2. Fill a third beaker with clean water.
3. Turn off the slurry diaphragm pumps, located at the right rear of the machine.
4. Locate the pH transmitter, mounted just above the diaphragm pumps.
5. Manually rotate the transmitter counterclockwise to unscrew it from its socket.
Note: The wire will remain connected.
6. Rinse the pH electrode in clean water.
7.
--[p313 [表]]-- Submerse the pH electrode into the pH 4 value buffer solution, gently stirring the solution for a few seconds, allowing the transmitter’s LCD display to stabilize.
8. While monitoring the transmitter’s LCD display, adjust the standard potentiometer:
GOAL #1: | The display must read within +/- 0.1 pH of 4 while the transmitter&#x27;s electrode is immersed in a pH 4 buffer solution.

===== [p166-169] SECOND TABLE POLISH POSITION SHOCK ABSORBER ADJUSTMENTS > C. ADJUSTMENT PROCEDURE (5块) =====
--[p169 [表]]-- C. ADJUSTMENT PROCEDURE
Readjust the large front shock absorber:
Note: This readjustment will throw the previous adjustment slightly off.
Turn the compressed air OFF.

--[p123]-- C. ALIGNMENT PROCEDURE
1. Select Right Spindle Speed and enter 0 to stop the spindle.
2. Open the operator doors.
3. Remove the indicator from the spindle.
4. Locate the four 3/8-in. socket head bolts mounted vertically inside the spindle clamp rings. Each bolt is secured by two 5/16-in. set screw and jam nut pairs.
5. Loosen the four bolts and the eight set screw/jam nut pairs:
a. Using a 1/2-in. open end wrench, loosen all eight jam nuts by rotating them counterclockwise.
b. Using a 5/32-in.
--[p124 [表]]-- Manually rotate the spindle to a position nearest the bolt registering the lowest measurement.
12. While watching the dial indicator, rotate the bolt clockwise until the indicator reads within +/- .001 in. of the readings at the other three points.
GOAL: | The dial readings should be within +/- .001 in. of equal as the spindle rotates.
13. Using a feeler gauge, measure the gap at the bolt between the two clamp rings.
--[p125]-- FINAL GOAL: | The dial readings at all four points should be within +/- .001 in. of equal as the spindle rotates. and
The gap between the two clamp rings at each of the four points must be between .030 in. and .060 in.
Note: You may have to go back and forth among the bolts, repeating the adjustments until the final goal is met.
15. When the final goal has been met, tighten the eight set screws to just snug by rotating them clockwise.
CAUTION: Overtightening will stretch the top clamp ring.

===== [p264-264] LOAD CHUCK VACUUM SENSOR ADJUSTMENT > ROBOT (3块) =====
--[p264]-- ROBOT
Version 4.0 of the 6DS-SP Operations and Maintenance manuals addresses the “RTZ” robot which has replaced the pre-3/95 "two arm" robot. The letters "RTZ" represent the three axes of motion called "Radial", "Theta", and "Z". However, 6DS-SP displays and user documentation will use the terms "arm", "rotate" and "up/down" respectively.
--[p264]-- For robot calibration, be sure to follow the Elevators and Robot - Order of Adjustment, located at the beginning of the Elevators section, above in this chapter.
For calibration of a two arm robot when Software Version 4.00 or later is installed on your machine, follow the procedures found in Version 2.0 of the 6DS-SP Maintenance manual, substituting the detailed keystroke instructions (which match pre-4.00 software) found there with post-4.00 software commands.
--[p264]-- Note that although the user interface has changed, the tasks and goals are essentially the same. Refer to the 6DS-SP User Interface Reference in Appendix A of the 6DS-SP Maintenance manual or Version 4.0 of the 6DS-SP Operations and Maintenance manuals for detailed information on using the 4.00 software interface. For extended descriptions of 6DS-SP calibration variables, refer to the Calibration Variables List found in Appendix A of Version 4.0 the 6DS-SP Maintenance manual.

===== [p31-33] ASSEMBLY AND DISASSEMBLY OF A CARRIER > E. INSTALL INNER/OUTER GIMBAL RING UNIT ONTO WAFER MANIFOLD PLATE (7块) =====
--[p31]-- E. INSTALL INNER/OUTER GIMBAL RING UNIT ONTO WAFER MANIFOLD PLATE
1. Place the wafer manifold plate on the stainless steel workplate of the bench top carrier fixture or on a solid workbench surface, positioned with the four tapped flange holes facing up and the pin holes at the edges of the plate oriented at 3 o’clock and 9 o’clock.
(Refer to Figure 9-10, below.)
2.
--[p31]-- Place the inner/outer gimbal ring unit over the wafer manifold plate, positioning the unit such that the inside diameter flange bearings of the inner gimbal ring are at 3 o’clock and 9 o’clock, as shown in the figure below, and in alignment with the pin holes located at the edges of the wafer manifold plate.
3. Install inner spacers in the wafer manifold plate counterbores with the flanges of the spacers mating to the counterbores:
a.
--[p32]-- carefully set the inner/outer gimbal ring unit down onto the wafer manifold plate, aligning the pin holes and trapping the spacers.

===== [p197-197] MENUS USED IN MECHANICAL ADJUSTMENTS AND SOFTWARE CALIBRATION PROCEDURES > EASY SERVO CALIBRATION: (2块) =====
--[p197]-- EASY SERVO CALIBRATION:
The Manual Control, Calibration/Configuration, and Diagnostics Menus work together as a special group. If a user makes either Manual Control or Diagnostic menu changes, those changes will be maintained so long as the user remains within the three menu group. This permits easy servo calibration as shown in the example below.
To calibrate relationships between the robot arm and an elevator:
1. Select the Manual Menu.
2. Move the elevator to a desired slot.
3.
--[p197]-- Move the robot to the elevator position.
4. Move the arms into the elevator.
5. Change to the Calibration/Configuration Menu.
6. Change the calibration variables for elevator offset, robot position, and arm position as required until alignment is achieved. (Unreasonable values will be ignored, and a warning will show.)
The servo systems will immediately respond to the calibration changes you make.

===== [p284-292] AT THE LOAD STATIONS -- ROBOT ARM EXTENSION (RADIAL) AND TRAVEL (LINEAR) CALIBRATION > Notes: (8块) =====
--[p284]-- Notes:
The arm extension and linear robot positions are calibrated to position the end effector directly over the wafer center at the load stations. Arm extension "count" values for the RTZ robot will typically be approximately 40,000 to 50,000 where the two arm robot had values nearer to 3,000.
In a two table machine, the left load linear robot position must be significantly different for the RTZ robot from that of the two arm robot.
--[p292]-- If the arm is too near the robot carriage, move the arm away from the robot carriage by increasing the current value of the variable by 500- count increments.
The larger the count number, the farther the robot arm is extended from the robot carriage.
If the arm is too far away from the robot carriage, move the arm toward the robot carriage by decreasing the current value of the variable by 500-count increments.
--[p285]-- The linear robot should be positioned off center to the right of the load station to make sure the robot arm extends through the load station cutout. This position is actually a mirror image of the right load station calibration which always has the robot off center to the left.
--[p290]-- If the arm is too far away from the polish table, move the arm toward the polish table by increasing the current value of the variable by .01 to .1-inch increments.
If the arm is too near the polish table, move the arm away from the polish table by decreasing the current value of the variable by .01 to .1- inch increments.
1. Note whether the arm is positioned too near the polish table or too far away from the polish table.
2.
--[p291]-- At the Calibration/Configuration Menu increase/decrease the value of variable 107, Left load robot position, as needed to meet the goal:
a. Increase/decrease the variable value as needed.
b. Reevaluate the robot position, and readjust the variable value if needed.
c. Repeat checking and adjusting until the goal has been met.
--[p291]-- Notes:
If the RTZ robot is used on a two table machine, this position will be a distance to the right of the load station.
Nominal value for single table machines: - 10 in.   
Nominal value for two table machines: - 5 in.
Changing the value of variable 107 while the robot is in its left load position via the Manual Control Menu automatically repositions the robot to the new location.
3. Check the new position against the goal and repeat the positioning adjustment in smaller increments as needed.
4. Refer to the Summary Sequence, above, and, if needed, correct the positioning of the axis of lesser error.
--[p290]-- Notes:
The linear positioning is corrected by increasing or decreasing the value of the variable by .1-inch or smaller increments as needed. Make coarse adjustment by changing the variable value in .1-inch increments; make fine adjustments with .01-inch increments.
As noted earlier, home for the robot’s linear axis is 0. Positions at the load stations are always expressed in negative numbers.
--[p291]-- Notes:
The robot arm(s) radial positioning variable values are expressed in counts. A nominal value for the RTZ robot arm position variable is 50000.
The positioning is corrected by increasing or decreasing the current value of the variable in 500 count increments as needed. 500 counts is approximately equal to .1 inch.
Use the following guidelines when making adjustments:
The smaller the count number, the nearer the robot arm is to the robot carriage.

===== [p267-267] ROBOT UP/DOWN (Z-AXIS) TOP, MIDDLE, AND BOTTOM POSITIONS CALIBRATION > HOW THE ROBOT’S UP/DOWN MOTION IS USED AT THE ELEVATORS (3块) =====
--[p267]-- At the Receive Elevators - The robot up/down movements at the receive elevators permit the robot to extend its arm while holding a wafer into the middle of a cassette slot (middle position), turn vacuum off to release the wafer, and move up slightly above the wafer (top position) before retracting out of the slot. The bottom position is not used at the receive elevators.
Setting Goals for Cassettes with Slot Spacing Other than Those Listed Above and Processing of Other Wafer Sizes
--[p267]-- HOW THE ROBOT’S UP/DOWN MOTION IS USED AT THE ELEVATORS
At the Send Elevators - The robot up/down movements at the send elevators permit the robot to extend its arm into a cassette slot slightly above the waiting wafer (top position), move down to the wafer (bottom position), turn vacuum on to pick up the wafer, and move up slightly (middle position) before retracting out of the slot.
--[p267]-- Check the cassette slot spacing and make appropriate adjustments in the values for variables 116, 117, and 118 based upon the desired relationships between the three positions as shown in the two tables above.

===== [p76-77] ELEVATOR CASSETTE ARM SENSOR SWITCH ADJUSTMENTS > C. ADJUSTMENT PROCEDURE (2块) =====
--[p76]-- C. ADJUSTMENT PROCEDURE
1. Lift the sensor arm.
2. Locate the micro switch mounted at the end of the cassette sensor arm.
3. Loosen the two mounting screws:
a. While holding one screw firmly with a flat blade screwdriver, use a small adjustable wrench to rotate its nut counterclockwise.
b. Repeat for the other mounting screw.
4. Manually reposition the switch slightly.
5. Retighten each nut by rotating it clockwise while holding its screw with the screwdriver.
6. Lower the arm to test.
7.
--[p77 [表]]-- Check the adjustment by reading the cassette sensor input status for the left send elevator at the Diagnostics Menu:
GOAL: | When the cassette sensor arm is down, Input 37 should display ON.
(right send elevator | Input 38)
(left receive elevator | Input 39)
(right receive elevator | Input 40)
a. If the goal is met, repeat for each of the other three elevators.
b. If the goal is not met, make corrections by repeating the adjustment procedure above.

--[p345]-- This value is determined experimentally by entering values into counters 12 and 13 in the Diagnostics Menu with the spindles over cleaning stations and observing the resulting spindle forces. ===== [p200-200] MENUS USED IN MECHANICAL ADJUSTMENTS AND SOFTWARE CALIBRATION PROCEDURES > SLURRY ALARM ACTION CHOICE: (1块) =====
--[p200]-- SLURRY ALARM ACTION CHOICE:
Calibration variable 59 "Slry alrm action (0-no, l-yes)" permits assignment of certain actions to the presence of an alarm indicating low or absent slurry.
If set to "0", slurry alarms will display as information only.
If set to " 1 ", cycle starting will be inhibited if any polish step requires a slurry that has an alarm. If already in an auto cycle, a "finish cycle" will be automatically set if such an alarm occurs.
Finally, if not in a cycle, the alarm will still display as information only.

===== [p388-388] SLURRY DIAPHRAGM PUMP PRESSURE (2块) =====
--[p388]-- This adjustment should be the minimum pressure necessary to maintain slurry solution volume flow through the lines to the peristaltic pumps. Greater pressure than necessary could cause the delivery lines to expand from the increased load.
Note:
Be sure to complete the procedure below before doing the Slurry Flow Calibration procedure found in the Software Calibration Procedures chapter of this manual.
--[p388]-- SLURRY DIAPHRAGM PUMP PRESSURE
ÀDANGER
MOVING COMPONENTSCAN CRUSH BODY PARTS
keep hands and arms away from elevators, spindles, turrets, robots.
The two slurry pumps, located at the left rear of the machine, are air driven diaphragm pumps that "squeeze" slurry solution into the delivery lines.
Each diaphragm pump has an air regulator to adjust the volume flow of slurry solution.

===== [p72-72] ELEVATORS AND ROBOT-- ORDER OF ADJUSTMENT > Front to Rear (2块) =====
--[p72]-- Front to Rear
1. While holding one hand under the elevator support platform to provide support, use a 5/32-in. hex key to loosen the three 10-32 socket head adjusting screws by rotating them counterclockwise.
2. While continuing to support the platform with one hand, tighten all three adjusting screws until just snug by rotating them clockwise.
3. Referring to Figure 9-14, tighten adjusting screw B 1/8 turn farther.
4. Adjust screw A and screw B as needed to meet the goal:
--[p72]-- • To lower the end of the platform nearest the robot, rotate screw A clockwise.
• To raise the end of the platform nearest the robot, rotate screw A counterclockwise.
Note: If the goal cannot be met by adjusting screw A, screw B may have to be adjusted another 1/8 turn clockwise or as needed.

===== [p127-127] LEFT SPINDLE UP LIMIT SWITCH > C. ADJUSTMENT PROCEDURE (2块) =====

2.
--[p127 [表]]-- Find the upper limit switch and switch actuator for the left spindle, located at the front of the upper bridge and nearest the left spindle.

4. While watching the monitor screen, slide the switch actuator bar up or down in the slot as needed until the switch is tripped.
GOAL: | Input 1 should be ON when the spindle is in its up position.

===== [p399-399] SOFTWARE AND CONTROL COMPUTER MAINTENANCE > OVERVIEW (4块) =====
--[p399]-- (See also the Recipe Management Menu section of the Machine Setup chapter of the 6DS-SP Operations manual for information on storing and retrieving recipes for customized auto polish process cycles.) Because stored polish recipes are custom created by the facility process engineer or supervisor(s), until the user makes a backup copy set on diskettes, such unique and valuable polish recipes are extremely vulnerable.
--[p399]-- OVERVIEW
The chapter below provides details on hardware and software setup of the 6DS-SP control computer as well as procedures for backup, restoration, and management of critical files.
The 6DS-SP software control program is installed on the hard disk residing in the control computer, with replacement copies available on 3 1/2-in. or 5 1/4-in. diskettes as required from Strasbaugh.
The polish recipe files stored by the user on the control computer’s hard disk are unique.
--[p399]-- If not, read the chapters in this manual on Physical Description, Installation, Mechanical Description, Control System Description, Power Distribution, and Plumbing Description, as well as the Operator Functions and Machine Setup chapters of the 6DS-SP Operations manual, before beginning any procedure.
--[p399]-- To protect unique process information, make a backup each time you save a new polish recipe.
Assumption - The procedures below are discussed with the assumption that the reader is thoroughly familiar with the 6DS-SP Planarizer.

===== [p442-442] MACHINE HALTS DURING CYCLE WITH POWER STILL ON BUT MOTION SUSPENDED - PART B > Error Messages (1块) =====
--[p442]-- Error Messages
All error messages except Elevator Section Operator Door Open and Polish Section Operator Door Open are accompanied by alarm sounds.
The control computer displays one error message at a time; if multiple problems exist (typically unlikely), correct the one indicated by the first message. The next message will then appear. After that problem is resolved, the error message for the second problem will be displayed.

===== [p273-281] ROBOT ARM EXTENSION (RADIAL) AND TRAVEL (LINEAR) CALIBRATION > Notes: (11块) =====

--[p280]-- Notes:
The robot arm(s) radial positioning variable values are expressed in counts. A nominal value for the RTZ robot arm position variable at the elevator is 50000.
The positioning is corrected by increasing or decreasing the current value of the variable in 500 count increments as needed. 500 counts is approximately equal to .1 inch.
Use the following guidelines when making adjustments:
The smaller the count number, the nearer the robot arm is to the robot carriage.
--[p281]-- If the arm is too near the robot carriage, move the arm away from the robot carriage by increasing the current value of the variable by 500- count increments.
The larger the count number, the farther the robot arm is extended from the robot carriage.
If the arm is too far away from the robot carriage, move the arm toward the robot carriage by decreasing the current value of the variable by 500-count increments.
--[p277]-- The robot arm must be aligned within the target linearly (side to side) and positioned radially (in and out) with a .0625 in. (1/16-in.) gap between the end of the arm and the target outline at a point nearest the front of the machine.
a. If the robot arm position meets the goal, skip to When a Satisfactory Adjustment Is Achieved, below in this section.
b. If the arm position does not meet the goal, proceed to Adjustment Procedure, immediately below, to correct the positioning.

===== [p258-258] UNIVERSAL WAFER CASSETTE SUPPORT (5块) =====
--[p258]-- (Nominalnumber of dunk distance slots equals 3&quot; divided by cassette slotspacing.) Elevators will be &quot;unhomed&quot; if this variable is changed,requiring re-homing.
If any of the above variables is changed, the elevators will be "unhomed", requiring rehoming. This prevents any elevator movements until all values are changed to reasonable values.
Variable 84 is set to the actual slot spacing.
--[p258]-- Elevators will be &quot;unhomed&quot; ifthis variable is changed, requiring re-homing.
85 # of slots in cassette(REHOME) | The number of slots in the cassettes being used. Elevators will be&quot;unhomed&quot; if this variable is changed, requiring re-homing.
86 Dunk distance (slots)(REHOME) | The distance, expressed in number of slots, from the wafer loadingplane to just below the water level which is nominally 3&quot;.
--[p258 [表]]-- This distance is typically 3 inches; it can be calculated as follows:
Dunk distance = 3 " / Nominal slot spacing
The following table shows typical "dunk distance" values for common cassette slot spacings.
Cassette Slot Spacing | “Dunk Distance (in slots)
3/16 in. | 16
1/4 in. | 12
3/8 in. | 8
3/4 in. | 4
--[p258]-- (This might be slightly different from the nominal spacing due to manufacturing tolerances of a particular manufacturer's cassette. Wafer handling problems may occur if variable 84 is too different from the actual slot spacing.)
Variable 85 is simply set to the number of slots in the cassette.
Variable 86 represents the distance, expressed in number of slots, required to lower a slot from the wafer loading plane to a point just below the elevator tank water surface.
--[p258 [表]]-- UNIVERSAL WAFER CASSETTE SUPPORT
This features permits the 6DS-SP software to be adjusted for use of cassettes with any number of slots and any slot spacing (within the mechanical move limits of the elevators).

===== [p198-198] MENUS USED IN MECHANICAL ADJUSTMENTS AND SOFTWARE CALIBRATION PROCEDURES > OPTIONAL OPERATOR ACCESS TO POLISH TIME ANDBACKPRESSURE POLISH PARAMETERS: (1块) =====
--[p198]-- OPTIONAL OPERATOR ACCESS TO POLISH TIME ANDBACKPRESSURE POLISH PARAMETERS:
Calibration Variable 99 "Oper access(0-no, l-T, 2-T&BP)” can be used to permit access to certain polish parameters even if the Operator password level is set.
The choices are: 0- No access to any polish parameters
1- Access to polish times only
2- Access to polish times and backpressure values
If any access is permitted, any change will cause the Rec (recipe) area of the screen to indicate MOD (modified).

===== [p194-194] SOFTWARE CALIBRATION PROCEDURES > OVERVIEW (2块) =====
--[p194]-- OVERVIEW
The Software Calibration Procedures chapter provides step-by-step instructions for factory-performed procedures for software calibration of the bridge, cleaning stations, conditioning arm, elevators, load stations, robot, slurry system, spindles, and polish table(s).
In addition, the section on Menus Used in Software Calibration presents details on the three menus (Manual Control, Diagnostics, and Calibration/Configuration) used in machine maintenance and calibration.
--[p194]-- Assumption - The procedures below were written with the assumption that the reader is thoroughly familiar with the 6DS-SP Planarizer. If not, read the chapters in this manual on Physical Description, Installation, Mechanical Description, Control System Description, Power Distribution, and Plumbing Description, as well as the Operator Functions and Machine Setup chapters of the 6DS-SP Operations manual, before beginning any procedure.
Examples - Detailed examples are provided for all required calculations to aid the user in following the calibration procedures.

===== [p2-2] The Incoming Compressed Air Supply Filter and Regulation System (2块) =====
--[p2]-- The Incoming Compressed Air Supply Filter and Regulation System
The incoming compressed air supply filter and regulation system requires periodic inspection, with frequency depending on the quality of the air supply. The filter element should be visually inspected for contamination and replaced when inhibiting the air flow. A partially clogged filter will produce an excessive pressure drop which could eventually affect machine operation.
--[p2]-- The coalescing filter should be inspected for visible contamination and replaced if clogged with visible debris or if air flow is restricted. The bowl is self draining, and some fluid is usually visible. If the bowl is too full of fluid, and fluid is found in the air lines, replace it.

1. Clamp the dial indicator to the right spindle ball.

4. Adjust the indicator linkage to allow the indicator stylus to touch the table.

--[p118 [表]]-- Read the indicator dial at several points around the table as the spindle rotates.
GOAL: | The dial readings should be within +/- .001 in. of equal as the table rotates.
If the readings meet the +/- .001 requirement, no adjustment is needed.
If not, follow the procedures below to adjust the alignment.

===== [p232-233] ENHANCED CLEANING STATION ROTATIONAL SPEED (POTENTIOMETER) CALIBRATION > LEFT CLEANING STATION (3块) =====
--[p232]-- LEFT CLEANING STATION
1. Pull relay 35 out of its socket to disable the right cleaning station while calibrating the left one.
2. At the servo amplifier for the left cleaning station:
a. Set pot 1 (loop gain) fully counterclockwise.
b. Set pot 2 (current limit) fully clockwise.
c. Set left “slow” motor pot fully counterclockwise.
d. Adjust pot 4 (test offset) clockwise until the left cleaning station motor starts to rotate and then back off (rotate counterclockwise) until it just stops.
e.
--[p233]-- At the Diagnostics Menu, select Toggle Output and enter 3 to turn on Output 3 (Left Brush Up), raising the cleaning station brush.
(Right Brush Up = Output 4)
5. Adjust the left “fast” motor pot for desired brush rotation rpm in the cleaning mode. (Factory setting is approximately 150-200 rpm.)
6. At the Diagnostics Menu, select Toggle Output and enter 3 to turn off Output 3 (Left Brush Up), lowering the cleaning station brush.
(Right Brush Up = Output 4)
--[p232]-- Adjust the left “slow” motor speed pot fully clockwise, placing the motor into high rpm.
f. Adjust pot 3 (ref in gain) clockwise until no further increase in motor rpm is noticed; then back off (rotate counterclockwise) until the motor just starts to slow from max rpm.
Note: The potentiometers have now been calibrated for a full swing of the motor speed pot from 0 to 100% rpm.
3. Adjust the left “slow” motor pot for desired rpm in the idle mode. (Factory setting is approximately 30-50 rpm.)
4.

===== [p259-263] LOAD CHUCK VACUUM SENSOR ADJUSTMENT > Notes: (3块) =====
--[p259]-- Notes:
Wafer presence on a load chuck is determined by sensing the vacuum quality at the load chuck. High vacuum indicates all load chuck holes are blocked (wafer present). Low vacuum indicates that at least one load chuck hole is not covered by a wafer (wafer absent).
• Refer to the Manufacturer’s Documentation section of this manual for detailed information on the SUNX Digital Pressure Sensor.
--[p263]-- Notes:
A slight stabilization delay (typically one second) will be seen at several points in the automatic cycle after load chuck vacuum is applied. At the end of a manual cycle, wafer presence is briefly checked every five seconds. Thus, the load chucks will lower shortly after wafers are manually removed while leaving vacuum released most of the time, permitting the operator to pick up a wafer.
--[p263]-- • If the lines are full of water, you may need to let the lines clear by leaving vacuum on for several seconds with no wafers.
a. If the goals in Steps 5., 7., and 8., above in this section, are met, skip to When a Satisfactory Adjustment Is Achieved, below.
b. If the goals are not met, check for vacuum leaks or stoppages.

===== [p52-52] J. WAFER MOUNTING PLATE ADJUSTMENT - FOR THREE-, FOUR-, AND FIVE-INCH CARRIERS ONLY > Obtain the Pocket Depth Specification (1块) =====
--[p52]-- Obtain the Pocket Depth Specification
The pocket depth is process-specific. The desired depth must be determined by the thickness of the wafers to be processed, the thickness of the insert material used, and the amount of wafer extension required.
In addition to adjusting the wafer backing plate, you may also insert shims for additional adjustment of pocket depth.
Note that shims are available in .002-in. and .003-in. thicknesses.

===== [p49-50] ASSEMBLY AND DISASSEMBLY OF A CARRIER > I. INSTALL CARRIER TOP PLATE (4块) =====
--[p50]-- Install a carrier seal into the two grooves of the wafer side of the carrier.
15. Using isopropyl alcohol, clean the carrier seal and the entire face of the carrier.
--[p49]-- I. INSTALL CARRIER TOP PLATE
1. Remove the two pivoting retainers.
2. Remove the locking block.
3. Hold the carrier top plate concave side down over the carrier assembly and oriented such that the swivel elbow of the top plate is at 6 o’clock.
4. Install the open end of the top plate’s 1/4-in. tubing on the barb of the manifold plate elbow.
5. Place the top plate concave side down on the carrier assembly.
6. Align the two top plate shoulder screws at 3 o’clock and 9 o’clock.
7.
--[p49]-- Check to see if the carrier is fitted with a target.
a. If the carrier is not fitted with a target skip to Step 8., below.
b. If the carrier is fitted with a target, rotate the top plate 90 ° to align the hole in the top plate with the target.
c. Go on to Step 8., immediately below.
8. Align the four 8-32 holes in the top plate with the corresponding holes in the carrier unit.
9. Install the appropriate bit on the power screwdriver.
10.
--[p50]-- Set the power screwdriver for approximately 15 inch-pounds of torque.
11. Install the four 8-32 x 1/2 in. screws in the four 8-32 holes:
a. Insert the four screws into the holes.
b. Using the power screwdriver, tighten the screws to approximately 15 inch-pounds of torque.
12. Remove the carrier from the maintenance fixture.
13. Place the carrier on a solid workbench surface positioned with wafer mounting side (the side with the small holes) up.
14.

c. Using the channel lock pliers, remove the tube fitting from the elbow.
d. Remove the elbow by turning it counterclockwise with an adjustable wrench.
2.
--[p135]-- If there is a bolt in the center of the table, remove it by using a 3/4-in. box end wrench.
Leave the washer in place.
6. Install a 1/2-13 NC eye bolt at the center of the table. Screw the eye bolt at least ten turns clockwise to secure.
7. Open the Right Side Operator Door.
8. Remove the white nylon crane mounting cap located to the left front of the table.
9. Install the Strasbaugh table hoist crane in the crane mounting slot with the crane suspended over the table.
10 Hook the chain of the crane into the eye bolt.
Activate the jack and raise the table:
--[p135]-- By hand, rotate the table counterclockwise to move the second tube fitting to the front of the machine.
3. Repeat Steps 1b, 1c, and 1d to disconnect the second line and associated fittings.

--[p21]-- Install new insert on carrier:
8. Install the two insert alignment pins (supplied by Strasbaugh with the machine) in the two alignment holes--one on each side of the wafer mounting plate.
9. Peel back the backing past center on the new insert, exposing more than half of the pad (such that it will clear the two alignment notches).

11.

13. Remove the alignment pins.

15. Working from the previously placed portion of the pad, smooth the remaining pad into place.

===== [p451-452] MACHINE HALTS DURING CYCLE WITH POWER STILL ON BUT MOTION SUSPENDED - PART B > Notes on Bridge Shutoffs Due to Low Sensed Spindle Vacuum: (3块) =====
--[p451]-- Notes on Bridge Shutoffs Due to Low Sensed Spindle Vacuum:
The following scenario will cause a bridge “following error” even though there is nothing wrong with the servo system.
1. The bridge is attempting to move.
2. A spindle vacuum switch is off even through the spindle vacuum is on.
(The cause would probably be a misadjusted vacuum switch or low supply vacuum.)
3. The software thinks it has lost a carrier and disables the bridge amplifier.
4.
--[p452]-- If this is described in the error log, troubleshoot the spindle vacuums and not the servo system.
Note: Opening and closing a polish door will reset the servo after this error.
--[p452]-- The servo controller notices that the bridge motor is not going where it is supposed to, assumes trouble, and turns off the motor in a control sense.
The end result is an error such as “Bridge not arriving at load” showing, and a servo status with the motor off and the motor error on.
When this occurs, the error log will show the vacuum error immediately (no matter how brief it was) and the bridge move error ten seconds later.

===== [p114-114] PERISTALTIC PUMP LINEREPLACEMENT > Line Replacement Procedure: (1块) =====
--[p114]-- Line Replacement Procedure:
1. Turn the machine power to OFF by pressing the red <EMERG OFF> button located on the control panel.
2. Turn off the slurry diaphragm pumps at the pump valves, located at the right rear of the machine.
3. Open the Polish Area Right Side Operator Door.
Open the pump head by popping the retainer clip off.
5. Loosen the two hose fittings mounted on the manifold, beneath the pump head.
6. Remove the fittings from the tubing.
7. Remove the tubing from the pump head.
8.
Replace with a new section of tubing.
9. Reinstall the fittings.
10. Close the pump head.
11. Turn the diaphragm pumps on.
12. Power up the machine.

===== [p140-140] POLISH TABLE REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION > Remove Table Pad and Clean Table (1块) =====

===== [p408-408] STARTING THE 6DS-SP CONTROL PROGRAM AT THE DOS PROMPT (2块) =====
--[p408 [表]]-- STARTING THE 6DS-SP CONTROL PROGRAM AT THE DOS PROMPT
To start the 6DS-SP control program at the DOS prompt after such procedures as formatting diskettes or backing up, follow one of the two methods below:
1. Method 1:
Operator Action Explanation/Screen Display
a. <Ctrl> <Alt> <Del>
While holding down the Ctrl key and the Alt key, press the Del key.
b. Wait.
Wait for the control computer to reboot and display the Main Menu screen.
--[p408]-- When the control computer is ready, the screen will display the 6DS-SP Main Menu.
2. Method 2:
Operator Action Explanation/Screen Display
F <Enter>
Type “F” to restart the 6DS-SP control program.
When the control computer is ready, the screen will display the 6DS-SP Main Menu.

===== [p308-309] SLURRY SYSTEM > B. CHECK THE CURRENT CALIBRATION (2块) =====
--[p309 [表]]-- Calculate the actual flow:
ACTUAL FLOW I | Flow Amount / Flow Rate
Example:
ACTUAL FLOW | 1800÷ 3.75
ACTUAL FLOW | 二 480 ML/MIN
GOAL: | ACTUAL FLOW = Programmed Flow Rate test value.
If the ACTUAL FLOW is not equal to the Programmed Flow Rate test value, adjust the calibration as shown in the Adjustment Procedure section below.
If the ACTUAL FLOW is equal to the programmed flow rate test value, go on to the When Satisfactory Adjustment Is Achieved section (below).
In our example, our programmed flow rate is 600 ML/MIN and our ACTUAL VALUE is 480 ML/MIN, therefore we must adjust the calibration.
--[p308]-- B. CHECK THE CURRENT CALIBRATION
1. At Page 3 of the Manual Control Menu, enter a programmed flow rate test value for Slurry Flow 1 of 600 ML/MIN.
2. Open the Right Side Operator Door.
3. Place a 2000 ML graduated beaker under the slurry tube. Close the door.
4. Time the flow:
Begin timing as the flow hits the bottom of the beaker.
a. Time the period it takes to fill the beaker to 1800 ML. Flow Amount = 1800 ML
b. Record the Flow Rate. Example: 3 min. 45 sec. (3.75 min.)
5.

===== [p198-198] MENUS USED IN MECHANICAL ADJUSTMENTS AND SOFTWARE CALIBRATION PROCEDURES > MANUAL CONTROL MENU: (1块) =====
--[p198]-- MANUAL CONTROL MENU:
The Manual Control Menu supports every servo move used by the machine including elevator stepping. In addition, this menu supports virtually everything required for machine calibration (for example, backpressure, end effector vacuum, and load chuck raising and lowering).
Also, once a servo move has been requested, it will be repeatedly asserted until changed or otherwise canceled, permitting easy servo calibration.

--[p214]-- Many of the calibration variables have numerical limit protections to prevent potentially damaging values. For example, every servo calibration variable has this protection. A warning will show if an illegal entry has been made.
Note also that this menu will not permit changing bridge calibration values if the spindles are not up. A warning will show if this is attempted.

--[p214]-- CALIBRATION/CONFIGURATION MENU
This menu permits entry of values related to machine calibration and configuration. Calibration includes the adjustments made by technicians (servo positions, force scale factors, etc.). Configuration includes settings that either must be a certain way depending on machine options (second table installed, etc.) or settings that are seldom changed (units of force measurement, etc.).

--[p61]-- C. ALIGNMENT PROCEDURE
1. Using a 9/16-in. socket wrench, loosen the four hex head bolts at the base of the cleaning station by rotating each counterclockwise.
2. Tap on the side of the cleaning station with the largest gap, moving the station in the direction that will lessen the gap.
3. Re-measure the gaps.
4. Tap and remeasure, repeating until the measurements meet the goal.
5.
--[p61]-- When the goal has been met, tighten the four bolts at the base of each cleaning station by rotating them clockwise to firm.
6. Close the Left Side Operator Door.
7. Raise the left spindle:
7. At Page 2 of the Manual Control Menu, select Left Spindle Up/Down and choose Up to raise the left spindle.
(right spindle = “Right Spindle Up/Down”)
8. At Page 1 of the Manual Control Menu, select Shuttle Move and choose Front to move the shuttle assembly to its forward position.

===== [p201-201] MANUAL CONTROL MENU > MANUAL CONTROL MENU (SCREEN PAGE 1) (3块) =====
--[p201]-- MANUAL CONTROL MENU (SCREEN PAGE 1)
This menu/page permits manual manipulation of every system involved with wafer handling. If an illegal choice is made, a warning will show. If any choice is made, Stat: (status) will change to Manual Mode.
If the entry area shows a dashed line, then a choice has not yet been made. If an entry area shows a choice, then that choice will be continuously asserted (with the exception of elevators).
--[p201]-- This can sometimes be useful for error recovery or to advance a send elevator past many empty slots. However, it is possible to move elevators to positions at which the robot arm can strike a wafer on the next cycle -- THEREFORE, USE CAUTION! (For maximum safety at the "operator" password level, attempting to move an elevator will make it "inactive", and the Auto Cycle will no longer use the elevator until it is reset by raising its arm.)
--[p201]-- For example, if the bridge was commanded to move to the load position but is stopped because the polish door is opened, the bridge will continue on to the load station when the door is closed.
The status of any item having either servo position checks or physical switches is shown to the right of the selection area.
If the machine is idle, it is possible to move elevators that are "active" to positions which are different from those at the end of the last polish cycle.

===== [p200-200] MENUS USED IN MECHANICAL ADJUSTMENTS AND SOFTWARE CALIBRATION PROCEDURES > SCRUBBER SUPPORT: (1块) =====
--[p200]-- SCRUBBER SUPPORT:
This feature supports a scrubber station at the right receive position which can pass wafers to a wafer scrubber. The 6DS-SP communicates with the scrubber using six handshake signals connected to 6DS-SP digital inputs and outputs. The 6DS-SP outputs are buffered with relays.
Several alarm conditions are supported and displayed. If the scrubber becomes unavailable, the 6DS-SP will direct polished wafers to the receive cassette.

===== [p43-44] ASSEMBLY AND DISASSEMBLY OF A CARRIER > 22. Torque each jack screw to 120 inch-pounds using a torque wrench: (3块) =====
--[p43]-- 22. Torque each jack screw to 120 inch-pounds using a torque wrench:
a. Attach a 7/8-in. crowfoot to the torque wrench.
b. Set the torque wrench at 120 inch-pounds.
c. Place a 1/2-in. open end wrench on the 1/2-in. square head of one jack screw.
d. While using the 1/2-in. open end wrench to hold the jack screw place the torque wrench crowfoot on the lock nut and tighten the nut to 120 inch-pounds of torque (until the wrench clicks).
e.
--[p44]-- Check the height of the jack screws again with the indicator in position and make final adjustments with a 1/2-in. open end wrench while observing the indicator for the exact setting.
--[p43]-- Remove the torque wrench and the open end wrench from the jack screw and its lock nut.
f. Repeat Steps c. through e., immediately above, for each of the other two jack screws.

===== [p349-349] WAFER BLOW OFF PRESSURE CALIBRATION > Notes: (1块) =====
--[p349 [表]]-- Notes:
The range allowed for setting blow off pressure is 0 to 55 psi.
If the pressure is set below 15 psi, the wafer may not blow off the carrier; if the pressure is set above 45 psi, the carrier may blow off the spindle.
The recommended initial setting is 30 psi.
GOAL: | The wafer must blow off the carrier every time, and the carrier must never blow off the spindle.
At the Calibration/Configuration Menu, enter a value for variable 170, Wafer blow off (psi) of 30.

===== [p307-307] SLURRY SYSTEM > AWARNING (1块) =====
--[p307]-- AWARNING
SLURRY COMPOUNDS MAYCAUSE INJURY
Use appropriate caution for the slurry currently in use. Refer to suppliers' material safety data sheets.
Slurry flow is determined by the shaft speed of the peristaltic pump motor. The head of the peristaltic pump is designed to pump a fixed volume of fluid per shaft revolution. The actual flow rate also depends on the size of the tubing used for the slurry delivery lines, tubing age, and flow resistance in the slurry line plumbing.
Calibration therefore becomes necessary. Calibration is performed by adjusting the peristaltic pump motor shaft speed.

===== [p143-143] POLISH TABLE REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION > 7. Adjust the jack screws: (2块) =====
--[p143]-- 7. Adjust the jack screws:
a. Adjust the jack screw next to the lowest point (the lowest indicator reading) by rotating it clockwise 1/8 turn with a 1/4-in. hex key.
b. Re-zero the indicator at the previous 0 line.
c. Rotate the table counterclockwise and read the dial at each line.
d. Repeat the process of adjusting the jack screws, re-zeroing the dial indicator, and re-taking the readings, making adjustments as needed to all 3 jack screws until the goal is met.
--[p143]-- Note: If the screws get too tight, you may have to loosen them slightly.
8. When the adjustment is satisfactory:
a. Remove the dial indicator.
b. Replace the Lower Right Front Service Door.
c. Replace the splash ring.
d. Close the Right Side Operator Door.
e. Rotate the Compressed Air Supply valve 1/4 turn counterclockwise to turn the compressed air supply ON.
f. Turn the machine power to ON by pressing the green <MACHINE ON> button located on the control panel.
g.
Following the procedures found in the Operator Functions chapter of the 6DS-SP Operations manual, home the machine.

===== [p41-42] ASSEMBLY AND DISASSEMBLY OF A CARRIER > Goal for Six-Inch Carriers Only: (3块) =====
--[p41 [表]]-- Goal for Six-Inch Carriers Only:
GOAL: | Each jack screw must protrude within +/- .001 in. of .140 in. beyond the bottom side of the plate.
a. Set the indicator on the manifold plate.
b. Turn the indicator ON.
c. Move the indicator to a location near one of the jack screws.
d. Zero the indicator.
e. Move the indicator to the horizontal surface of the jack screw to measure the protrusion (height ) of the jack screw from the manifold plate.
f. Read the indicator gauge.
--[p42]-- If the reading meets the goal, skip to Step h., below in this section.
If the reading does not meet the goal, correct by following the procedure in Step g., immediately below.
g. Correct the position of the jack screw by hand rotating it from the bottom while reading the gauge.
Rotate the jack screw as needed until the goal is met.
h. Repeat Steps b. through g., immediately above, for each of the other two screws.
--[p42]-- When all three jack screws meet the positioning goal, go on to the step immediately below.
17. Release the pivoting ring retainers.
18. Rotate the manifold assembly 180 \_ to reposition the assembly with the square heads of the jack screws protruding down.
Note: The round ends of the jack screws will be facing up.
19. Relock the pivoting retainers.
20. Without turning the jack screws, carefully place an O-ring seal on the back of each.

Note: The left of the two columns is cooling water “in.”
COOLING WATER
Flow
I/O 22.8 23.2 degC
2. Calculate the temperature in scale factor:
SCALE FACTOR = Actual Temperature / COOLING WATER (IN) (from control unit (from screen) display)
Example:
SCALE FACTOR = 20 ÷ 22.8
SCALE FACTOR = .877
3.

===== [p2-2] The Drain Tubs for the Polish Table and Elevator (1块) =====
--[p2]-- The Drain Tubs for the Polish Table and Elevator
The drain tubs for the polish table and elevator should be frequently checked and periodically cleaned out to prevent the drain hoses and piping from clogging. ===== [p274-274] ROBOT ARM EXTENSION (RADIAL) AND TRAVEL (LINEAR) CALIBRATION > Required Positions for Robot Arm Extension (1块) =====
--[p274]-- Required Positions for Robot Arm Extension
To permit the robot to safely extend its arm (move radially), the robot’s Z-axis must first be in a up/down position, as shown below:
· At the send elevators, the robot must be at its up/down top position.
· At the receive elevators, the robot must be at its up/down middle position.

===== [p186-186] RESTORATION OF LOAD CHUCK HEIGHT TO THE PREVIOUSLY MEASURED POSITION > 5. Right load chuck: (1块) =====
--[p186]-- 5. Right load chuck:
a. Using a 9/16-in. open end wrench or 9/16-in. universal socket wrench, loosen the two 3/8-16 hex head bolts mounted on the vertical surfaces of the load station adapter plate by rotating them counterclockwise.
b. Using the precision scale to measure and the 1/2-in. key stock and the feeler gauges as needed to shim up the load chuck, raise the load chuck to the down position height recorded before disassembly.
c. Using a 9/16-in. open end wrench or 9/16-in.
universal socket wrench, retighten the two 3/8-16 hex head bolts to firm by rotating them clockwise.

===== [p187-187] RESTORATION OF ELECTRICAL POWER FOR THE SECOND TABLE > B. PROCEDURE TO RECONNECT 588, 589, AND 590 (1块) =====

===== [p117-117] PERISTALTIC PUMP LINEREPLACEMENT > Remove Table Pad and Clean Table (1块) =====
--[p117]-- Remove Table Pad and Clean Table
1. Lift and remove the white plastic splash ring from the table.
2. Use a plastic scraper to raise one edge of the pad.
3. Peel the pad off by rolling to the opposite edge.
4. Discard the used pad.
5. Clean and dry the table with a soft cloth:
a. Feel the table by hand for adhesive residue.
b. Remove remaining residue with mild solvent.
c. Dry with soft cloth.
